We then obtain the scattering matrix, its unitarity and a two-channel optical theorem. The main result is a uniqueness theorem for the inverse problem. Under two geometric conditions on the pair, the scattering amplitude at a single positive energy determines the perturbation completely, and the argument does not distinguish a deformation of the boundary from an obstacle. It follows that no nontrivial perturbation satisfying the same conditions is invisible at any positive energy. On the surface band the corresponding statement is reduced to one explicitly stated question about the exterior Robin problem.

title: Failure of noncommutative Rota's theorem with $L\log L$ endpoint
summary: We construct a factorizable Markov map $T$ on a hyperfinite finite von Neumann algebra and a positive element $x\in L\log L$ for which the sequence $T^n(T^*)^n x$ does not converge bilaterally almost uniformly. This answers a question of Anantharaman-Delaroche \cite{AD2006}.

title: An Approximate-Diagonal Characterization of Amenable Actions on C*Algebras
summary: We introduce relative $h$-diagonals for crossed products $A\rtimes_αΓ$ by discrete groups, which are positive-form approximate diagonals in the Haagerup tensor product taken relative to $A$. We show that $α$ is amenable if and only if $A\rtimes_αΓ$ admits a relative $h$-diagonal, an analogue of Johnson's theorem for $L^{1}(G)$.

title: Graph-Recurrent Learning of Emergent Collective Dynamics
summary: Collective ordering in correlated electron systems emerges from microscopic dynamics, yet the evolution of observable textures need not admit a closed, memoryless description. We introduce a graph-recurrent neural network (GRNN) framework that learns such emergent dynamics directly from trajectories without specifying microscopic equations of motion. The framework integrates gated recurrent memory with graph message passing: local hidden states encode information beyond the instantaneous observables, while spatial coupling allows this information to propagate between sites. The observable and hidden fields evolve jointly through a shared local rule, providing a scalable representation of dynamics with spatial interactions and temporal memory. We demonstrate this framework on the emergent dynamics of charge-density-wave order in the semiclassical Holstein model, successfully reproducing temporal and spatial correlations and dynamical scaling during domain coarsening. By learning finite-time evolution directly, the GRNN offers a route to efficient, data-driven descriptions of collective dynamics with unresolved microscopic degrees of freedom.

title: Interaction-enhanced antiferromagnetic correlations in a Kondo ladder with a gapped band structure
summary: We investigate magnetic correlations in the two-leg Kondo-Hubbard ladder using the density-matrix renormalization group method. We focus on a parameter regime in which the noninteracting electronic system has a narrow indirect band gap. In this regime, there is no Fermi surface, and the conventional Fermi-surface-based Ruderman-Kittel-Kasuya-Yosida picture is not directly applicable; magnetic correlations between localized spins become weaker as the noninteracting band gap increases. We find that a moderate on-site Coulomb interaction enhances the antiferromagnetic correlations between localized spins. This enhancement, which is also seen in the staggered magnetization induced by a pinning field at the edges, occurs for both ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic Kondo couplings. Our results show that electron-electron interactions can enhance magnetic correlations between localized spins even when the underlying noninteracting electronic structure is gapped, suggesting an interaction-driven route to magnetic instabilities in narrow-gap Kondo-lattice systems.

title: Fit-error corrected auxiliary master equation approach for low-temperature nonequilibrium dynamical mean-field theory
summary: The auxiliary master equation approach (AMEA) is a nonperturbative impurity solver for steady-state nonequilibrium dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT). It replaces the physical hybridization function by that of a small auxiliary open quantum system, whose parameters are fitted to reproduce it, and then solves the resulting many-body problem essentially exactly. AMEA's accuracy is thus limited by the quality of this fit: since the fastest-varying part of the hybridization is set by the distribution function, whose Fermi edges sharpen at low temperature, the fit tends to overestimate the temperature, especially for weak reservoir coupling. For the auxiliary hybridization itself, however, AMEA's self-energy is essentially exact. We correct for the fit error by estimating, via an approximate solver applicable to arbitrary hybridization functions, the ratio between the self-energies of the physical and auxiliary hybridizations, and using it to extend AMEA's self-energy from the auxiliary to the physical case. This fit-error correction becomes exact whenever either the fit or the approximate solver is exact. We benchmark the scheme using the nonequilibrium Kajueter-Kotliar iterated perturbation theory (IPT), generalized here to spin-polarized solutions, as the approximate solver; other approximate solvers, such as the noncrossing approximation, can be used as well. Applied to an Anderson impurity model with a spin-polarized bath, and within DMFT to a Hubbard layer weakly coupled to two metallic reservoirs, the correction largely removes the spurious heating from the AMEA fit and from insufficient thermalization by the reservoirs, while preserving the correct description of the Mott insulator, which IPT alone cannot fully recover.

title: Anyon Chern bands of opposite sign and reversed drift
summary: The elementary charged excitations of fractional quantum Hall states are anyons. Without continuous translation symmetry, they acquire a dispersion and richer dynamics. We study the Laughlin quasihole at filling $1/3$ in a periodically modulated magnetic field, a common model of fractional Chern insulators in two-dimensional materials. From the microscopic wave functions, we derive the commutator of its guiding-center coordinates, set by a many-body Berry curvature that governs its wave packets. A modulation with two flux quanta per unit cell splits the quasihole band into bands with Chern numbers $6$ and $-3$; such opposite signs are generic as long as a weak modulation opens a gap between the anyon bands. In the $C=-3$ band, the quasihole drifts against $\mathbf{E}\times\mathbf{B}$, although the magnetic field has the same sign everywhere. Perturbation theory in the modulation explains these results, and large-scale Monte Carlo calculations confirm them. Anyon bands thus acquire their own topology, which controls anyon motion and may shape the phases of itinerant anyons.

title: A signature of the timelike singularity in holography
summary: In the context of the AdS/CFT correspondence, we provide a simple observable, the imaginary part of the retarded Green's function, which captures the timelike singularity of a charged black brane. Solving wave equations of bulk fields with different spins outside the black brane, we calculate exponentially small contributions to retarded Green's functions in the dual CFT at large real frequency. These contributions admit an interpretation in terms of paths in an analytically continued classical black brane interior via a WKB approximation: they provide the complex time elapsed along null geodesics that reflect off the singularity, and incorporate the corresponding reflection coefficients.

title: Random Euclidean CFT$_2$ from Triangulated dS$_3$ Gravity
summary: We propose a random Euclidean CFT description of three-dimensional de Sitter gravity, with fixed central charge and primary spectrum but fluctuating operator product coefficients. Our construction starts from compact regions assembled from generalized hyperbolic tetrahedra. We analytically continue the gravitational amplitudes computed from these triangulations to de Sitter parameters and use them to infer OPE correlations. We recover matching normalized amplitudes from a complex Liouville cosmological wavefunction. A non-Gaussian fourth moment encodes the hyperbolic core volume in an oscillatory semiclassical phase. We construct the associated Lorentzian de Sitter spacetime and show that derivatives of this phase recover its boost holonomies. Its spacelike future boundary carries a positive-definite conformal metric, while the wavefunction obeys Euclidean conformal Ward identities. These relations connect the proposed OPE statistics to both the Euclidean boundary description and the Lorentzian bulk geometry. Integrating the absolute square of the cosmological wavefunction over boundary moduli gives cosmological observables. Their long-collar factorization reproduces the edge measure of the two-matrix model.

title: Hydrodynamic description of correlation matrix eigenvalues in a finite temperature expanding free fermionic gas
summary: A recent work considered the Page curve for entanglement entropy of a freely expanding one-dimensional Fermi gas starting from a finite box (the system) in a zero-temperature initial state that then expands in to a semi-infinite vacuum (the environment). For the case with a single defect at the system-environment junction, it was shown that the Yang-Yang entropy of the system computed from semiclassical hydrodynamics agrees with the microscopically computed entanglement entropy, yielding the Page curve. On the other hand, the environment Yang-Yang entropy showed a monotonic increase. Here, we propose a hydrodynamic description to obtain the eigenvalues of the microscopic correlation matrix for a nonzero temperature freely-expanding Fermi gas. For the system, the phase space density directly gives the correlation matrix eigenvalues and thus, via the Yang-Yang formula, yields the von-Neumann entropy. For the reservoir, a modification of the phase space density is required in the Yang-Yang formula, to incorporate coherences, in order to reproduce accurately the entropy. The hydrodynamic description of correlation matrix eigenvalues also leads to a Levitov-Lesovik type formula for the full-counting-statistics for a finite system in the transient regime. We provide a heuristic derivation of the correlation matrix eigenvalues based on a semiclassical wave-packet picture.

title: Generalized Coordinate Bethe Ansatz and Quantum Integrability of the Time-Dependent Massive Thirring Model
summary: We develop a generalized coordinate Bethe-ansatz framework for the massive Thirring model with an explicitly time-dependent fermion mass. Unlike the generalized Bethe ansatz for chiral quantum field theories, where particle transport acts in internal spin spaces and leads to quantum Knizhnik-Zamolodchikov equations, the present construction acts directly on particle coordinates and physical rapidities. Its central new feature is a rapidity lattice. Because the time-dependent mass couples right- and left-moving components already in the one-particle sector, a fixed-rapidity block is not closed under spatial winding. Periodicity therefore requires all sectors generated by the finite shift $β\toβ-p$. Particle exchange relates amplitudes on this lattice through scalar analytic difference equations of Ruijsenaars type, whose solutions determine the complete time-dependent many-body wavefunction. Consistency of the coordinate construction also selects an exponential evolution of the bare mass, providing a new realization of the time dependent integrability-renormalization group correspondence. In the static limit, the rapidity-lattice construction reduces to the conventional massive-Thirring Bethe equations. Through the massive-Thirring/sine Gordon equivalence, the result also connects this exact quantum construction to the generalized space-time dependent Lax formalism.

title: Carrollian Symmetries and Dynamical Entropy
summary: Carrollian geometry has recently emerged as the proper language to understand the geometry of null hypersurfaces from an intrinsic perspective. In this paper, we demonstrate that the Noether charge associated with the intrinsic conformal symmetry of Carrollian manifolds yields exactly the dynamical entropy formula recently proposed by Hollands, Wald and Zhang. This result follows directly from the requirement that the gravitational phase space induced on a finite distance null hypersurface be anomaly-free, in a covariant phase space sense. We then show that a linearized perturbation of this dynamical entropy charge, sourced by an external matter perturbation falling across the hypersurface, satisfies a physical process first law. Moreover, upon imposing the classical null energy condition, a linearized second law holds for the dynamical entropy. We then turn to a semi-classical generalization of this construction, where we argue that a notion of dynamical generalized entropy follows from considering perturbations sourced by external quantum matter. By imposing the quantum null energy condition (QNEC), we find a generalized second law for a linearized perturbation of the dynamical generalized entropy. Finally, we use our results to speculate on relations to the quantum focusing conjecture.

title: Semiclassical effects on ultramassive spacetimes
summary: A recent work [Senovilla, Port. Math. 80 (2023)] has shown that accretion of matter by a Schwarzschild-de Sitter black hole can take this object beyond a critical limit where the event and cosmological horizons coalesce, transforming it into a collapsing universe resembling a Kantowski-Sachs cosmology. In these configurations, dubbed ``ultramassive spacetimes'', future asymptotic infinity and the event horizon associated with the black hole cease to exist. In this work, we take the first steps toward exploring semiclassical gravity effects on such geometries. In particular, we examine the fate of Hawking radiation in these backgrounds and analyze the behavior of the renormalized stress-energy tensor within the Polyakov approximation. We also explore the effect of semiclassical backreaction on the evolution of the horizons, focusing on cases in the vicinity of the extremal limit, and on the subsequent universal collapse.

title: Fermion Hierarchies from Fricke Modular Symmetry
summary: We show how Fricke modular symmetry can generate realistic fermion hierarchies and quark CP violation from a single modulus in a supersymmetric effective theory. Matter fields are labelled by the two one-dimensional characters of $Γ_0^+(N)$ that are trivial on $Γ_0(N)$, and interactions use complete spaces of cusp-regular holomorphic modular forms. At level three, the Fricke extension enlarges an interior stabilizer from order three to order six, allowing its parity to enforce three additional powers of the displacement $t$. An explicit assignment gives quark mass powers $(7,3,0)$ and $(5,4,2)$ and CKM powers $(1,2,3)$. The leading textures conserve CP, but an exact relation among the modular generators produces an appreciable CKM phase at finite displacement. A fit at $|t|\simeq0.306$ reproduces the quark and lepton reference values with order one coefficients in a fixed normalization. We also relate the Fricke double-coset algebra to coset non-invertible symmetry; on the coefficient spaces used here its action reduces to ordinary Fricke parity.

title: Mellin Moments of Proton Unpolarized GPDs at Nonzero Skewness from Lattice QCD with a Neural-Network Parametrization
summary: We use lattice QCD to determine the generalized form factors (GFFs) entering the first four Mellin moments of the unpolarized isovector $u-d$ proton GPDs at nonzero skewness. The framework combines the polynomiality of the moments in the skewness $ξ$, with the short-distance expansion formalism, allowing the lattice-extracted reduced Ioffe-time distributions (ITDs) to be expressed in terms of GFFs. In order to extract the GFFs by fitting these relations to the lattice data, we parameterize each GFF with an artificial neural network (ANN) as a continuous function of the invariant momentum transfer squared $t$, which accommodates the kinematic coverage of the data in a flexible way. With this fit, we determine the fourteen GFFs that enter the first four Mellin moments, including the skewness-dependent GFFs. From the extracted GFFs, we obtain the quark total angular momentum of the isovector combination, $J^{u-d}=0.296(11)(7)$ in the $\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$ scheme at $μ=2~\mathrm{GeV}$, in agreement with previous lattice determinations based on nonlocal operators and with a smaller total uncertainty. We also determine the impact-parameter distributions of the first three Mellin moments in an unpolarized and in a transversely polarized proton. We finally identify and discuss the principal systematic uncertainties which enter this extraction, and the challenges specific to the nonzero-skewness regime.

title: Scalar-scalar-graviton vertex from Asymptotic Safety
summary: The unitarity and causality properties of asymptotically safe quantum gravity are still unsettled. Scattering amplitudes provide a direct test, but their computation requires fully momentum-dependent correlation functions. In this light, we compute the full scalar-scalar-graviton vertex from Asymptotic Safety within a mostly analytic approximation. Qualitatively, we find the expected logarithmic branch-cut structure, and we correctly recover the double-eikonal soft divergences predicted by Weinberg's soft theorem. Quantitatively, we find that non-minimal operators are generally as important as the minimal vertex stemming from the scalar kinetic term.

title: Adapted Fröhlich-Pizzo Model for Horizon-Induced Decoherence
summary: The Fröhlich-Pizzo (FP) model is a quantum-mechanical model originally developed to describe the interaction between an atom and the electromagnetic field in the nonrelativistic limit $c\to\infty$. We show that an adaptation of the FP model based on the local algebras of a $U(1)$ chiral current captures essential features of the horizon-induced decoherence mechanism identified by Danielson, Satishchandran, and Wald (DSW) in the limit of large holding time $T$. Our analysis suggests that the effective dynamics of the system undergoing decoherence in the DSW setting retains non-Markovian features. Our approach also offers a glimpse into the possible role of quantum events in the dynamics underlying horizon-induced decoherence.

title: Rotation slows the instability of Ellis-Bronnikov wormholes
summary: We present nonlinear 3+1 evolutions of rotating Ellis-Bronnikov wormholes. We construct stationary rotating drainhole solutions with a spectral solver up to an equatorial rotation velocity of 99% of the speed of light, validate the solver against published symmetric solutions, and correct an inconsistency in a published field equation. Perturbed only by truncation error, the evolutions show that rotation slows the radial instability of the static wormhole. Near 30% of the extremal angular momentum the unperturbed throat expands instead of collapsing, rather than the instability disappearing as second-order perturbation theory suggests. From 58% upward we find no evidence of instability over the evolved times; at the fastest spin this holds at three resolutions. Collapsing rotating throats emit an axisymmetric quadrupolar gravitational-wave burst whose energy grows with spin. Second-order perturbative initial data trigger the instability through their own truncation error, so they are unsuitable for stability studies.

title: An end-to-end function for the photograph of a Schwarzschild black hole
summary: We show that the photograph of a Schwarzschild black hole can be written in closed form. The image plane is embedded as a plane tangent to a sphere centred on the black hole, and the map between a point source and its image point, which we call the photograph function, is treated as the analytic object. Explicit expressions are obtained for sources on the celestial sphere at infinity and for sources in the equatorial plane, without solving for the intermediate null geodesics. The construction is exact, and it makes the multivalued branch structure, the relation to the photon sphere and to the shadow boundary, and the self-similar higher-order images directly readable.

title: Wormholes in Vegh--dRGT massive gravity: a null-energy transparency theorem, horizon obstruction, and exact isotropic solutions
summary: We study static, spherically symmetric wormholes in deRham--Gabadadze--Tolley massive gravity with the spatially degenerate Vegh reference metric. The effective fluid carried by the massive graviton contributes nothing to the combination of density and radial pressure that the flare-out condition constrains, so it is invisible to the null energy condition along radial light rays. This holds for the whole degenerate class of reference metrics, for all four interaction potentials, and for any static spherically symmetric geometry; the same property singles out the Vegh choice as the only consistent one. The matter alone must therefore violate the null energy condition at every throat, exactly as in general relativity. This corrects a claim repeated across the massive-gravity wormhole literature. We then determine where throats may sit. Wormholes with isotropic pressure fall into two families. One lies beyond the cosmological horizon of the theory's own vacuum and has no static exterior; it is empty in general relativity and is switched on by the graviton coupling. The other lies inside that horizon and needs a steeply falling redshift. We give exact perfect-fluid solutions for both. In the second family the graviton term can turn the tension at the throat into ordinary pressure. A thin shell closes the configuration, and its surface stresses and its exotic-matter content follow in closed form. The shells are radially unstable, and light rays near the throat trace an unstable circular orbit.

title: Harmonic branches of Einstein--Maxwell--scalar field gravity: exact solutions and regularity
summary: We relate black-hole horizons and wormhole throats to the geometry of the harmonic branches of Einstein--Maxwell--dilaton gravity. In the unified Ernst framework, we first solve the harmonic equations prior to fixing the spatial harmonic, and then jointly reconstruct the metric, Maxwell four-potential, and scalar field. The conserved geodesic energy fixes the meridional Weyl quadrature, whereas the initial geodesic data capture the asymptotic charges. Choosing the Schwarzschild harmonic function, regular nonextremal horizons fix the normalization \(H=1\) along with the associated matter-field regularity requirements. This reproduces the Schwarzschild and Reissner-Nordstrom families (including the NUT extension), the Gibbons-Maeda solution, and the dyonic string and Kaluza--Klein solutions, while also preserving their more general branches. If the scalar sector is continued to the phantom sign, one obtains a complementary oblate construction: smooth continuation selects \(H=-1\) and produces the massive and ultrastatic Ellis-Bronnikov wormholes. By comparing with the vacuum ring geometry, we make clear the further importance of the global extension. Altogether, these findings offer a unified black-hole--wormhole geometric reading of the charge relations and regularity constraints for the reconstructed solutions.

title: Pure dephasing destroys two-photon amplitude, not nonlinear phase
summary: A two-level emitter chirally coupled to a waveguide imprints a $π$ conditional phase on a two-photon pulse, a key component assumed in quantum photonic neural network architectures, but whether it survives the pure dephasing of a solid-state emitter is unknown, since no two-photon scattering treatment includes it. We derive the dephased two-photon amplitude in closed form and validate it against an independent Fock-state master equation. The conditional phase is pinned at exactly $π$ at every dephasing rate examined: dephasing destroys the amplitude carrying the nonlinear phase rather than rotating it. The one- and two-photon channels are not attenuated equally, so dephasing does not simply scale the node down but reweights it between photon-number sectors---an error no phase setting can train away. The standard factorization of two-photon correlators, exact for arbitrary loss, fails at first order in $γ_φ$, discarding $16$--$81\%$ of pairs over $γ_φ/γ=0.1$--$1$.

title: Injection is all you need: parallel universal logic in high-rate concatenated self-dual codes
summary: We propose a quantum architecture that achieves addressable and parallel universal fault-tolerant logical in high-rate codes. The codes are obtained from the flexible concatenation of small-distance high-rate self-dual CSS codes. Addressable and parallel universal logic on the resulting $K$ logical qubits is injected by fault-tolerantly preparing and then consuming diverse logical $K$-qubit CSS stabilizer states and logical $\lvert H \rangle^{\otimes K}$ global magic states. Flag-at-origin is used to prepare the stabilizer resource states while a concatenated cultivation protocol prepares the global magic states. These resource states are consumed by Steane-QEC or Knill-QEC teleportation gadgets, which simultaneously perform quantum error correction. Any quantum algorithm with $T$-depth $D_T$ can be executed by consuming $12D_T$ or fewer resource states. We benchmark the fault-tolerant preparation of the resource states for several two-level concatenations of the $[[k+4,k,2]]$ H codes and the Hamming $[[15,7,3]]$ code. In particular, we find that the concatenated cultivation offers at least one order of magnitude spacetime reduction compared to cultivation in the surface code.

title: A random sampling method to test the weak Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis
summary: We introduce a random sampling method for testing the weak Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis (wETH) that is particularly useful for large, sparse Hamiltonians. We test the method on a well-studied Rydberg atom system that exhibits both two- and three-body dipole-dipole interactions. Our results show that our method allows for the study of system sizes significantly beyond the limits of exact diagonalization. We find that the fluctuations in eigenstate expectation values decay as the Hilbert space dimension $D^{-1/2}$, consistent with wETH and in agreement with previous numerical results.

title: High-fidelity and robust controlled-Z gates for superconducting transmon qubits. I. Intrinsic errors and decoherence
summary: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires quantum gates that combine short duration, high fidelity, and robustness to noise. As quantum processors scale, robustness becomes increasingly important because exhaustive characterization and frequent recalibration of individual gates become impractical. We present a comprehensive optimal-control framework for controlled-Z (CZ) gates between directly coupled, frequency-tunable transmons that systematically accounts for intrinsic Hamiltonian errors and realistic decoherence mechanisms, including energy relaxation and dephasing. Using smooth, single-shot flux pulses, we obtain 12-ns CZ gates---close to the theoretical speed limit of 11.6 ns---with intrinsic errors suppressed to the $2\times10^{-5}$ level. We construct dephasing noise models, calibrated against published experimental measurements, that capture fast dephasing from room-temperature control electronics and slow dephasing from $1/f$ flux noise. Using these models, we identify dephasing sweet spots that suppress sensitivity to dephasing noise. We further exploit transmon asymmetry as a design parameter to access distinct noise-resilient operating regimes. These results establish an experimentally applicable framework for balancing gate speed, fidelity, and noise robustness while reducing characterization and recalibration overhead.

title: Finite Classification of Transversal Diagonal Gates Beyond Stabilizer Codes
summary: We establish that transversal diagonal gates on exact qubit codes of distance at least two can be exhaustively classified within a finite search space. Although code-preserving physical gates can have continuous phases, any projective logical action induced by a transversal diagonal gate can always be realized by a physical gate of finite order. Crucially, we prove that this physical order has an upper bound determined solely by the code parameters. This order bound enables the subset-sum-linear-programming (SSLP) framework introduced in arXiv:2504.20847 to exhaustively enumerate all candidate discrete symmetries, after which the Knill-Laflamme equations determine the remaining continuous code parameters. Applying this method to the nontrivial diagonal sector of exact $((6,2,3))$ codes, SSLP yields $66$ candidate symmetry classes, of which exactly $15$ are realizable, supporting full projective diagonal logical cyclic groups of orders $2$, $3$, and $5$. In particular, for order $5$, the code is unique up to local unitaries and qubit permutations, equivalent to the code constructed in arXiv:2504.20847. This code also attains the minimum length $n=6$ among exact $((n, 2, \ge 3))$ codes whose full projective transversal group cannot be conjugated into the projective Clifford group.

title: Resource Analysis of Quantum Optimization Algorithms via Variational Methods
summary: Variational Quantum Algorithms (VQAs) are promising approaches for solving combinatorial optimization problems on near-term quantum devices. However, the role played by quantum resources such as entanglement and coherence during the optimization process remains poorly understood. In this work, we investigate the evolution of these resources in two VQAs--the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) and the Feedback-based Algorithm for Quantum Optimization (FALQON)--applied to the Minimum Vertex Cover problem. We employ a variational resource-quantification framework based on the Bures metric and Uhlmann's theorem, in which an auxiliary quantum circuit is optimized to identify the closest resource-free states. This approach allows us to quantify Bures entanglement and Bures coherence of the algorithmic states without requiring full quantum state tomography. For the considered problem instance, QAOA exhibits a pronounced accumulation of entanglement in its initial layers, followed by a progressive reduction as the algorithm converges toward the optimal solution. Its coherence likewise decreases overall with increasing circuit depth, although a finite residual value persists due to the degeneracy of the optimal-solution subspace. In contrast, FALQON exhibits a substantially lower entanglement peak, reached at larger circuit depth, followed by a decay as convergence proceeds. Its coherence decreases smoothly and monotonically together with the optimization error. These results reveal distinct quantum-resource trajectories associated with the two optimization strategies and illustrate how entanglement and coherence evolve as variational quantum states approach solutions of a classical combinatorial optimization problem.

title: Mamba Quantum Eigensolver (MQE): A Selective State Space Model for Scalable Ground State Simulations in Quantum Chemistry
summary: Predicting molecular electronic structure using Quantum Computing approaches is a challenge in Computational Chemistry. Traditional Variational Quantum Eigensolvers (VQEs) are typically hindered by optimization challenges. The alternative Generative Quantum Eigensolver (GQE) mitigates this by reformulating ground-state search as discrete sequence generation, but its Transformer backbone suffers from quadratic computational complexity, bottlenecking scalability for larger molecules. To address this, we introduce the Mamba Quantum Eigensolver (Mamba-QE), which replaces the Transformer with a Selective State Space Model (SSM) to process operator sequences with linear $\mathcal{O}(L)$ complexity. Additionally, we integrate a distance-conditioned mechanism enabling the direct prediction of complete potential energy surfaces (PES). Evaluated on the $H_2$ molecule, Mamba-QE reproduces Full Configuration Interaction (FCI) reference energies well within chemical accuracy, achieving an energy error below $3\times10^{-6}$ Ha across 16 geometries with zero variational violations. Mamba-QE maintains high expressive power while establishing a robust, scalable foundation for quantum simulations of complex molecular systems.

title: Quantum f-divergences from retrodiction: a unifying classical variational principle
summary: The same classical f-divergence admits inequivalent extensions to quantum states. The question is whether these extensions can be obtained from a common operational variational principle. Here we generalize Matsumoto's reverse-test optimization by introducing a reference prior state. More explicitly, we minimize the statistical distinguishability between a forward and a reverse prepare-and-measure process, related by retrodiction through the chosen reference and subject to prescribed quantum averages. Distinguishability is quantified by the classical f-divergence between their complete records. For faithful states in finite dimension, we prove that the same spectral implementation attains the minimum simultaneously for every operator-convex f. Varying the reference allows us to interpolate between standard and maximal quantum f-divergences of the prescribed states, passing through the geodesic family. More precisely, a flat reference yields the standard quantum f-divergences, thereby giving the Nussbaum-Szkoła distributions a variational characterization as optimal records. Choosing either prescribed state as reference recovers maximal quantum f-divergences and Matsumoto's reverse tests, while power references realize the geodesic interpolation. In the relative-entropy case, this gives the passage from Umegaki to Belavkin-Staszewski relative entropy by changing the prior for retrodiction.

title: Splitting Probability in Monitored Quantum Dynamics
summary: We consider a continuous-time quantum walk stroboscopically subjected to projective measurements on two distinct targets with sampling time period $τ$. We construct a general renewal framework for the first-detection amplitude at each target, from which we obtain the associated splitting probabilities. For Hamiltonians with reflection symmetry, we further show that each dual-target first-detection amplitude can be viewed as an interference effect between a pair of single-target first-detection amplitudes. This formulation yields exact expressions for the splitting probabilities and gives special sampling times at which they undergo pointwise discontinuous jumps due to a form of ergodicity breaking associated with dark states. As an illustrative example, we apply the framework to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice chain with nearest-neighbor hopping, and study the splitting probabilities as functions of the initial position and sampling time. Below a critical sampling time, $0<τ< τ_c$ where $τ_c = 2 π/ ΔE$ with $ΔE$ being the energy bandwidth, the splitting probabilities for large system sizes become equal to $1/2$, independent of the initial position, as long as this position does not coincide with target sites. Above the critical sampling time, $τ\geq τ_c$, the splitting probabilities deviate from $1/2$ and develop oscillations as a function of initial position. The wavenumber associated with these oscillations is $Q=2\sin^{-1}(rτ_c/τ)$, where $r$ is a positive integer. We also explore the effects of relative phase and spatial separation between different components of a coherent initial state on the splitting probabilities. Finally, we study how a finite number of measurements modifies the splitting probabilities and broadens the resonances at special sampling times.

title: Short qudit triorthogonal codes from doubling
summary: We construct short triorthogonal codes for qudits of odd prime dimension by generalizing doubling, which combines a triorthogonal code with a code admitting a transversal phase gate, and raises the distance by up to two. This gives codes with parameters $[[28,1,4]]_3$, $[[37,1,5]]_3$, $[[72,1,6]]_3$, $[[118,1,8]]_3$, $[[33,1,5]]_5$ and $[[20,1,4]]_7$, each shorter than the cyclic, concatenated and Reed-Muller codes of the same distance, and a doubling construction of the $[[15,1,3]]_3$ code. When the columns of a generator matrix are regarded as charged points, triorthogonality becomes the vanishing of multipole moments up to octupole order, and doubling becomes a double layer of opposite charges; this picture explains why inputs with nontrivial coefficients can give shorter codes. We also show by exhaustive search that the shortest codes of distance three have length $11$ for $p=5$ and length $7$ for $p=7$. Combined with high-rate distance-two codes, the new codes reduce the cost of qutrit magic state distillation by up to an order of magnitude in regimes with high input noise.

title: Quantum Simulation of Non-Markovian Open Quantum Systems via Low-Rank Kernel Compression and Coupling Dilution
summary: We present an error-controlled framework for the quantum simulation of non-Markovian open-system dynamics in Gaussian environments. For a system coupled linearly to a Gaussian environment with zero mean, the bath's influence on the reduced dynamics is completely determined by its two-time correlation kernel. This allows us to replace the microscopic environment with an equivalent bath that has the same kernel. On a finite simulation interval, a rank-$N$ approximation of the kernel yields an effective bath of $N$ bosonic modes with time-dependent couplings to the system. To encode these modes in qubits, we first truncate each mode to its lowest $d$ occupation levels. When stronger couplings lead to large occupations, we introduce coupling dilution, which replaces each mode with several more weakly coupled copies while preserving the bath correlation kernel. This distributes excitations across more modes and trades additional modes for smaller local dimensions. We derive explicit reduced-state error bounds and establish polynomial circuit width and depth in simulation time and inverse accuracy under stated spectral-decay and coupling-regularity assumptions, provided elementary unitaries admit polynomial-cost implementations.

title: Turning Quantum Compiler Configuration Selection Upside Down: A Top-Down Paradigm
summary: Selecting an effective quantum compiler configuration requires coordinated decisions over both hardware targets and compiler settings, with the ultimate goal of improving circuit execution fidelity. Existing SOTA approaches typically decompose this problem into two sequential stages: a device is chosen first, after which compiler options are tuned on that device through RL-based search. This bottom-up strategy can be fundamentally limited by its initial device decision, since a poorly matched backend may constrain the best fidelity achievable regardless of how effectively later compiler options are optimized. In contrast to classical compiler tuning, where the search space is often prohibitively large, the configuration space of quantum compilers remains manageable enough to support exhaustive search. Consequently, rather than repeatedly searching from candidate configurations, one can derive reusable configuration knowledge from offline oracle results and apply it directly to new circuits.   In this paper, we introduce a top-down configuration-selection paradigm and build QuOPTBench, an exhaustively searched benchmark containing oracle configurations for 268 quantum circuits. We first study whether LLMs can directly infer suitable configurations and evaluate ten representative LLMs. The results reveal that vanilla LLMs remain far from the oracle. We then employ an LLM to extract transferable rules from sampled circuits governing configuration selection. Using these rules together with predictors trained on the enumerated configuration data of the sampled circuits, we design QuTOP, a rule-guided ML framework that performs fast configuration selection without iterative online search. Across our evaluation, the distilled rules consistently strengthen LLM-based selection, while QuTOP provides the strongest overall balance between solution quality and selection latency among the baselines.

title: Evaluation of the quantum Fisher information for large systems via an ancilla
summary: Quantum Fisher information (QFI) is a fundamental quantity in quantum information and quantum mechanics, and evaluating it in various physical systems has become an important research topic. However, its evaluation in large systems still faces many challenges. Hereby we propose an ancilla-based protocol for evaluating the QFI of large systems and establish the conditions under which this protocol can ``perfectly'' evaluate the QFI in theory. As a demonstration, the protocol is applied to quantum circuits to evaluate the QFI of the Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger state.

title: Fast Template Matching for Quantum Circuits Using Hypergraph
summary: Quantum circuit optimization is a key step toward the efficient execution of quantum algorithms. Template matching has emerged as one of the dominant approaches for simplifying quantum circuits, yet it confronts the intrinsic challenge of accommodating gate commutativity. The state-of-the-art template-matching algorithm relies on a directed acyclic graph (DAG) representation. While this DAG-based technique handles gate commutativity satisfactorily, it fails to preserve the local connectivity inherent to quantum circuits, thereby leading to relatively high matching complexity.   In this paper, we introduce a hypergraph representation (HG), a commutativity-aware representation that collapses commuting gates into a single super-node while retaining all local connectivity. This enables matches to be extended locally without revisiting the rest of the circuit, with incremental updates limited to the immediate neighborhood. Experimental results demonstrate that our HG matcher achieves 11--606x speed-up over the DAG-based implementation in Qiskit (Iten et al., 2022) on both random and arithmetic benchmarks, while maintaining the same optimization quality. The acceleration increases with circuit size, confirming that preserving locality and connectivity is the key to scalable quantum circuit optimisation.

title: Algebraic criteria for complete relaxation in autonomous and periodically driven open quantum systems
summary: We derive sufficient criteria that guarantee convergence of open quantum system dynamics to a unique long-time state independent of the initial conditions. We refer to this behavior as complete relaxation. Focusing on systems described by Gorini-Kossakowski-Sudarshan-Lindblad (GKSL) master equations on finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces, our approach uses only elementary mathematical arguments. For autonomous systems, we recover three previously derived relaxation criteria, which can be expressed as algebraic conditions on the Lindblad operators and the Hamiltonian entering the GKSL equation. For periodically driven systems, we obtain a new criterion involving a similar algebraic condition and a local continuity requirement on the time-dependent GKSL generator. This result implies an earlier criterion for complete relaxation formulated in Ref. [J. Phys. A 52, 43LT01 (2019)]. We also discuss implications of our approach for periodically modulated classical master equations, as well as extensions to driven systems without a periodicity constraint.

title: Buffer-Qubit-Based Quantum Circuit Allocation Method Against Crosstalk Attacks
summary: Quantum Multi-Programming (QMP) enables the simultaneous execution of quantum circuits from multiple users on a single quantum chip in cloud quantum computing services. However, QMP is vulnerable to crosstalk attacks, in which a malicious user deliberately induces crosstalk to disrupt other users' computations. As a countermeasure, prior work has proposed the use of buffer qubits, which remain idle and are allocated between quantum circuits to suppress the effect of crosstalk. Nevertheless, to the best of our knowledge, such countermeasures have not been publicly reported in production quantum cloud software. In this paper, we extend the QMP of OQTOPUS, open-source software that is already in production use for operating real quantum computers, with a buffer-qubit-based circuit allocation method. Experiments on a real device characterize the attack effect in terms of energy relaxation and dephasing, showing that observable degradation appears in dephasing characteristics of qubits adjacent to the attacker circuit. Based on this result, we release the proposed method as part of OQTOPUS and confirm that the buffer qubits are correctly reserved around the allocated circuits.

title: On unitary vertex operator algebras
summary: We prove that a conformal vertex algebra with a non-zero invariant Hermitian form is unitary as soon as it admits a non-zero positive energy module with a positive definite invariant Hermitian form. Using free field realizations, we deduce that the principal simple $W$-algebra $W_k(\mathfrak g)$ of a simple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$ is unitary for central charge $c\ge rank(\mathfrak g)+24\bigl((ρ|ρ^\vee)+\|ρ\|\,\|ρ^\vee\|\bigr)$, and, if $\mathfrak g$ is simply laced, for all $c\ge rank(\mathfrak g)$. Among basic Lie superalgebras which are not Lie algebras, the free field argument applies to $osp(1|2n)$ and $osp(2|2n)$. It shows that $W_k(osp(1|2n))$ is unitary for $c\ge n+\frac12$ and gives an explicit bound for $osp(2|2n)$. Next, we prove that if $\mathfrak s$ is an even $sl_2$-subalgebra of a simple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$ whose centralizer is not abelian, then the simple $W$-algebra $W_k(\mathfrak g,\mathfrak s)$ is unitary for at most finitely many $k$. We illustrate this on the $W$-algebras of $sl_{qm}$ attached to the nilpotents of Jordan type $q^m$: unitarity is possible only at two levels, and for $q=2$ it does occur at both. For instance, the $W$-algebra of $sl_4$ attached to the partition $2+2$ is unitary only for $k=-2$ and $k=-\frac32$. This fails for Lie superalgebras, as minimal $W$-algebras show, but still holds under stronger assumptions. Finally, we prove that a simple $W$-algebra $W_k(\mathfrak g,\mathfrak s)$ can be unitary for only finitely many $k$ if $\mathfrak g$ is a simple Lie algebra and $\mathfrak s$ is not a distinguished $sl_2$ subalgebra.

title: A spinor-adapted geometric approach to nonlinear Dirac systems on the Schwarzschild black hole background
summary: Building on our previous work, we extend the spinor-adapted geometric method for nonlinear Dirac systems from small perturbations of Minkowski spacetime to the Schwarzschild background. As a linear foundation, we establish integrated local energy decay estimates and an \(r^p\)-weighted energy hierarchy for spinor fields, adapting the physical-space approach of Dafermos and Rodnianski to the Dirac setting.   The main focus of the paper is nonlinear. We consider a semilinear tensorial wave--Dirac model motivated by the wave-gauge reduction of the Einstein--Dirac system and prove global small-data stability. A principal difficulty is the apparent loss of derivatives arising from the coupling between the first-order Dirac equation and the second-order tensorial wave equation. We overcome this difficulty through a spinor-adapted energy hierarchy that exploits the complementary roles of the Dirac-current energy and the spinorial wave energy. In particular, the nonlinear estimates are closed without requiring the top-order Dirac-current estimate.   The nonlinear analysis demonstrates that the spinorial structures remain essential on the black-hole background. The combination of Dirac-current energy, spinorial wave energy, Kosmann Lie derivatives, and the Clifford-algebraic null structure enables us to close the nonlinear estimates without imposing an independent null condition on the tensorial wave equation. Thus, the nonlinear closure relies fundamentally on structures intrinsic to the Dirac equation.   A second main result is the global small-data stability of the Maxwell--Dirac system in the Lorenz gauge on the Schwarzschild background, under a vanishing-charge assumption. This extends the nonlinear stability theory to a genuine gauge-coupled Dirac system and demonstrates the applicability of the spinor-adapted physical-space approach beyond the tensorial wave--Dirac model.

title: Widom asymptotics for spatial compressions of Schrödinger spectral projections
summary: We establish a Widom trace formula for spatial compressions of exact spectral projections of semiclassical Schrödinger operators. The potential is smooth near a compact classically allowed region, and the observation domain lies strictly inside that region. For every continuous spectral function with positive power decay at both endpoints, we obtain a trace formula at scale $h^{1-n}\log h^{-1}$ whose coefficient separates into a boundary integral and a universal spectral functional. This yields the exact von Neumann and Rényi entanglement asymptotics for every fixed positive order, and proves their universal ratios to the particle-number variance. The proof combines commutator estimates in every fixed positive Schatten class with a local trace formula obtained from a boundary-adapted normal form and a Hardy model. In dimensions $n\ge2$, a positive partition and the known variance asymptotic control the grazing contribution; in one dimension all boundary Fermi points are transverse. A harmonic-oscillator counterexample shows that continuity and weighted integrability alone are insufficient for the trace formula.

title: Roe algebras and coarse index maps for spaces with proper actions of {é}tale groupoids. II
summary: Building on the Roe algebra framework developed in the first paper of this series, we construct equivariant coarse index maps for locally compact Hausdorff spaces equipped with proper actions of {é}tale groupoids, with coefficients in any separable groupoid C* -algebra. The construction uses the coarse structures determined by the groupoid action and requires no choice of metric. By identifying Roe algebras of canonical modules with reduced crossed products, we prove that the Baum-Connes assembly map with coefficients factors through the coarse index map.

title: New matrix-weighted norm inequalities and extrapolation
summary: In this paper, we propose a new type of matrix-weighted theory and show the corresponding Rubio de Francia extrapolation theorems by means of noncommutative maximal inequalities. We introduce a new matrix $A_p$ condition following Volberg's geometric formulation, and characterize it via a noncommutative Hardy--Littlewood maximal inequality. We then establish a noncommutative analogue of Rubio de Francia's abstract extrapolation theorem for trace-finite von Neumann algebras. The argument extends to $L_\infty(\mathbb R)\bar\otimes M_d(\mathbb C)$ through pointwise matrix operations. This yields the desired extrapolation results for individual operators and maximal families, with applications to matrix-weighted boundedness of Calderón--Zygmund operators.

title: Extending Doi--Takeuchi correspondence to bimodules and noncommutative covers
summary: Doi and Takeuchi, and independently Blattner, Cohen and Montgomery, have exhibited a correspondence between cleft extensions of an algebra $U$ by a Hopf algebra $H$ and $H$-measurings on $U$ equipped with a compatible normalized 2-cocycle. Each cleft extension is isomorphic as an algebra, a left $U$-module and a right $H$-comodule to the crossed product algebra constructed from the measuring and the cocycle. Cleft $H$-extensions are a special case of $H$-Hopf-Galois extensions, describing noncommutative principal $H$-bundles with affine total and affine base space. Corings are used to describe noncommutative space covers, allowing a description of possibly nonaffine noncommutative spaces. We propose to describe the total space of a noncommutative $H$-principal bundle by an internal $E$-coring in $H$-comodules where $E$ is an $H$-comodule algebra which is itself $H$-Hopf-Galois. This article focuses on the cleft case.   As corings involve bimodules and morphisms of bimodules we extend the Doi--Takeuchi correspondence to bimodule $H$-comodules between cleft extensions on one side and bimodules of $H$-coinvariants equipped with bimodule $H$-measurings compatible with 2-cocycles on the other side. In fact, the correspondences for algebras and for bimodules are parts of a biequivalence of suitable bicategories defined in this article. As a corollary one obtains a correspondence between cleft $H$-extensions of corings and corings equipped with a nonabelian Čech 1-cocycle covalued in $H$.

title: $G$-crossed braided tensor categories of twisted modules
summary: Let $V$ be a strongly rational vertex operator algebra and $G\leq\operatorname{Aut}(V)$ a finite group. We prove Huang's conjecture that the categories of $g$-twisted $V$-modules, for $g\in G$, form a $G$-crossed braided fusion category. This category is faithfully $G$-graded, with tensor products representing the complete twisted intertwining operators of Du-Huang, the canonical pullback $G$-action, and crossed braiding. In particular, the associativity, coherence and rigidity required by the conjecture all hold.

title: Stabilizing and detecting electron fractionalization in the Hofstadter-Hubbard model
summary: Motivated by the recent progress in correlated Chern insulator physics in moiré systems, we investigate the half-filled triangular-lattice Hofstadter--Hubbard model and its electron fractionalization. Among various competing non-magnetic states, increasing the orbital flux stabilizes and broadens the $\mathrm{U}(1)_2$ chiral spin liquid phase in the Mott regime. In this exotic regime, the electron is fractionalized into gapped spinons and gapped chargons, whose effective bands are linked to the orbital flux. The convolution of the narrow spinon bands with the gapped chargon excitations produces rich and discernible structures in the electron spectral function and the density of states. These results not only identify the orbital flux as a control parameter for the detailed patterns of electron fractionalization and the nature of the Mott transition, but also provide the key spectral characteristics for the angle-resolved photoemission and scanning tunneling studies of the relevant systems, linking the free-particle band topology to intrinsic topological order in the correlated regime.

title: Quantics tensor trains for multiloop functional renormalization group in multiorbital impurity models
summary: The full frequency dependence of electronic interactions is central to dynamical correlations, but its numerical cost restricts multiorbital calculations. We formulate the multiloop functional renormalization group directly in the quantics tensor train representation, retaining all three independent vertex frequencies over broad ranges without an explicit high-frequency parametrization. Analytical tensor operators perform frequency transformations and internal summations without dense vertex intermediates. Multiloop corrections improve agreement of vertices and responses with independent references and reproduce the low-energy numerical renormalization group self-energy. Lower-temperature calculations resolve a quadratic frequency contribution to the analytically continued scattering rate. A degenerate two-orbital impurity exhibits distinct spin, orbital, and charge responses at fixed Hund coupling. In a compensated altermagnetic environment, an orbital-level splitting induces a local spin response despite zero magnetization of the unperturbed impurity. Increasing Hund coupling suppresses the orbital response while increasing its spin polarization. Renormalized one-particle propagation alone does not reproduce this strong polarization dependence. These results extend compressed multiloop calculations to dynamical correlations in multiorbital environments.

title: Chirality, Klein duality, and the stability of Kitaev spin liquids on the star lattice
summary: The star lattice hosts the Yao-Kivelson chiral spin liquid, an exactly solvable Kitaev spin liquid that breaks time reversal spontaneously and is non-Abelian or Abelian depending on the ratio of its two couplings. A density-matrix renormalization group study found that an added Heisenberg exchange leaves it a wide stability window for ferromagnetic but only a narrow one for antiferromagnetic Kitaev coupling. Using projective symmetry groups (PSGs) of fermionic partons, we show that the chirality is not a peculiarity of the solvable point: whenever the $π$ spin rotations act on the partons as in the exact solution (spin-gauge locking), a time-reversal-symmetric mean-field state has no amplitude on the triangles, at any range, so a Kitaev-type spin liquid on this lattice must break time reversal. The Abelian and non-Abelian liquids of both signs share a single chiral PSG, within which their transition is a band inversion. The Klein duality, which reverses the Heisenberg coupling, permutes the PSGs and leaves exactly the locked ones unchanged; a $Z_2$ spin-liquid phase mapped onto itself is therefore locked and, if it spans a connected range of couplings, contains a Kitaev point. Unprojected mean-field theory in Kitaev's Majorana representation treats both signs alike. Exact second-order perturbation theory about the Kitaev points locates the asymmetry: the triangles respond identically for both signs, whereas on the bonds between triangles the two off-diagonal Heisenberg terms create the same four visons and interfere constructively for antiferromagnetic and almost destructively for ferromagnetic coupling, admixing a low-energy four-vison state $82$ times more strongly on the antiferromagnetic side. The PSG results rest on a classification of $352$ $Z_2$ PSGs with spin-orbit-coupled amplitudes, which also identifies the fermionic partners of the known Schwinger-boson spin liquids.

title: Spin-Clifford Bundles and Spin Connections on the Hyperbolic Clifford Algebra - Part I
summary: We develop the theory of spinor fields associated with the hyperbolic Clifford algebra $\mathbb{R}^{H}=\mathcal{C}\ell(H_V)$, which is associated with hyperbolic space $H_V=V\oplus V^{*}$. Algebraically, we exhibit an explicit real primitive idempotent which, unlike the Lorentzian case, remains primitive after complexification and generates the ideal of Witten superfields. We also describe the chirality decomposition and the hyperbolic spin group. Geometrically, we construct a canonical hyperbolic spin structure on every oriented manifold, showing that no topological obstructions arise beyond orientability and we study the associated spinor bundles, spin-Clifford bundles and ideal spinor subbundles. Finally, we introduce the isotropic extension of an arbitrary linear connection to $TM\oplus T^*M$, which is always compatible with the hyperbolic metric, and the associated hyperbolic spin connection, whose well-definedness, compatibilities, curvature and explicit form are established, providing the geometric framework for Dirac operators on the hyperbolic Clifford algebra, which we will present in a forthcoming article.

title: TQFT gravity dual to the orbifold groupoid of Narain code CFTs over $\mathbb{Z}_4$
summary: In a companion paper arXiv:2610.26610, we classified the Narain conformal field theories obtained by gluing copies of the $A_3$ root and weight lattices along their $\mathbb{Z}_4$ discriminant group. For two hyperbolic pairs, this gives twenty-two even self-dual gluing codes, which fall into seven inequivalent theories at $c=\bar c=6$. In this paper, we develop the physical interpretation of this family and its connections to three-dimensional topological field theory. We show that all twenty-two codes are topological boundary conditions of a single abelian Chern-Simons theory. Its invertible symmetries, which include fractional $B$-field shifts, organize the boundaries into three orbits: free, mixed and torsion. Boundaries in different orbits are related only by gauging. We determine all gaugings of order at most four between the seven theories, by $\mathbb{Z}_2$, $\mathbb{Z}_4$ and $\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}_2$, with explicit twisted partition functions, and follow their effect on the spectrum and the current algebra. We then sum the Chern-Simons partition function over handlebodies at genus one and prove a finite Siegel-Weil identity, valid for any number of pairs. For two pairs, the handlebody sum is the uniform average over the free theories. Recovering the average over all twenty-two theories requires one additional contribution, a solid torus with the torsion lines along its core. For three or more pairs, we find that the handlebody sum is not a positive combination of code boundary states.

title: Normal Matrix Model and Hyperelliptic Curves
summary: We present a two-matrix model with a normal matrix with eigenvalues confined to contours in the upper half plane coupled to a Hermitian matrix. This generalizes the matrix model proposed by Jens Hoppe which corresponds to a single horizontal line. We solve the saddle point equations for several lines and show that the large-N free energy can be expressed in terms of hyperelliptic integrals. We show that the model describes a Coulomb gas in the presence of an infinite conducting boundary.

title: Thermomagnetic enhancement of conserved-charge correlations in a lattice-constrained PNJL model
summary: Conserved-charge correlations offer a promising probe of magnetic fields in strongly interacting matter. We investigate their magnetic response and the finite-density equation of state within a lattice-constrained three-flavor Polyakov--Nambu--Jona-Lasinio model. A thermomagnetic scalar coupling, inferred by Gaussian process regression from lattice QCD results for the average light-quark condensate, incorporates inverse magnetic catalysis into the effective interaction. Without fitting conserved-charge observables, the resulting framework substantially improves their magnetic-field dependence and crossover behavior compared with the fixed-coupling model. In particular, it captures the pronounced magnetic enhancement of the baryon--electric-charge correlation and related susceptibility ratios, supporting their use as QCD magnetometers. The comparison demonstrates that the medium dependence of the effective interaction is essential to describe this response within the model. We further calculate pressure Taylor coefficients through sixth order and reconstruct the pressure and baryon density at nonzero baryon chemical potential. Our results show that lattice information from a single chiral observable constrains a broad thermodynamic response, connecting inverse magnetic catalysis, conserved-charge correlations, and the equation of state in a common framework. This provides a lattice-constrained basis for investigating magnetic-field signatures and finite-density thermodynamics in QCD matter.

title: Amplified EFT corrections near exceptional QNMs
summary: We show that the ordinary expansion of EFT corrections to individual QNM frequencies breaks down at an exceptional QNM, and that these corrections become enhanced for near-exceptional QNMs. We give a brief argument for why this should generally happen, before numerically demonstrating this behaviour by calculating the $α'^3$ corrections to QNMs of equal-spin Myers--Perry-AdS$_5$ black holes. This calculation corresponds to $λ^{-3/2}$ corrections to the poles of the retarded Green's function in the boundary CFT, where $λ$ is the 't Hooft coupling. Treating the coalescing pair together, we calculate the leading $λ^{-3/4}$ splitting at the uncorrected exceptional point and the $λ^{-3/2}$ displacement of the exceptional point in temperature and angular velocity. The background derivative expansion can remain valid while the nondegenerate expansion of individual frequencies fails. We discuss the implications for the full response and for other areas of black hole physics.

title: Maxwell-Chern-Simons-Matter in AdS$_3$
summary: We study Maxwell-Chern-Simons theory on AdS$_3$ coupled to $N$ complex scalars or Dirac fermions, including sextic and Gross-Neveu interactions, respectively. First, we derive the bulk Maxwell-Chern-Simons propagator, clarifying how Dirichlet boundary conditions fix the contributions of the massive and flat sectors. Upon coupling to the matter sector, we work at large $N$ with $κ=k/N$ and $α=Ne^2$ fixed, where $k$ is the Chern-Simons level. We determine the corresponding phase diagrams, and we resum matter insertions to obtain the photon propagator at leading order in large $N$, exactly in $α$ and $κ$. Its poles determine the spin-one boundary spectrum, split into two helicity sectors by the Chern-Simons interaction. With Dirichlet boundary conditions, the unHiggsed scalar phase contains a protected chiral current, which is lifted by Higgsing. In the fermionic phases, the current persists for nonzero effective Chern-Simons level, with helicity determined by the induced level shift. At bulk conformal points, we extract large-$N$ BCFT data for the critical and tricritical scalar theories, as well as for the regular fermion and Gross-Neveu theories.

title: Fluids on null hypersurfaces and Carrollian hydrodynamics
summary: We study intrinsic ideal fluids on null hypersurfaces and their realisations by causal fluids living in the ambient spacetime. An embedded null hypersurface is equipped with an induced Carrollian structure with a temporal Weyl symmetry inherited from rescalings of the null generator, and we develop the corresponding null submanifold and variational calculus. The intrinsic fluid phases are classified according to their realisation of Carroll boosts and temporal Weyl symmetry. If we demand that an ambient fluid be confined to a null hypersurface, the ambient fluid velocity must be null, which realises an intrinsic zero-temperature Carrollian phase with unbroken Carroll boosts. In general, timelike or null ambient fluids will cross a null hypersurface and lead to an open Carrollian system. On a null foliation, the sources correspond to transport between null leaves. We then show that there exists a decoupling limit of a timelike ambient fluid which gives rise to an autonomous Carrollian fluid with spontaneously broken Carroll boosts and no source terms. This decoupling limit corresponds to an infinite boost while keeping the enthalpy finite and nonzero, which leads to a divergent ambient energy-momentum tensor. Nevertheless, the induced Carrollian responses do not see the divergent term and remain finite, and an independent Carroll boost Goldstone emerges from a subleading component of the ambient fluid velocity in this limit.

title: 3D de Sitter from complex Virasoro TQFT: Observers and knots
summary: The Euclidean saddles of 3D Einstein gravity with positive cosmological constant are spherical three-manifolds. When one adds a heavy observer, the backreacted saddles are spherical cone manifolds, with a conical singularity along the observer worldline. We propose exact gravitational partition functions at fixed topology on a class of spherical cone manifolds that undergo hyperbolic-to-spherical transitions as the cone angles increase. Our construction relies on a careful analytic continuation of the product of two Virasoro TQFT partition functions. We test the proposal by showing that the exact partition functions exponentiate in the semiclassical limit to the spherical volume, in agreement with the gravitational on-shell action. This leads to a spherical volume conjecture for the product of continued Virasoro TQFT amplitudes. As further evidence, we relate the theta and tetrahedron graph amplitudes to the two-point function and out-of-time-ordered four-point function of operators on a massive observer's worldline. In appropriate limits, we recover the static patch scalar two-point function with finite observer backreaction and the semiclassical effects of observer recoil. In addition, we analyze examples with knotted worldlines and reproduce their spherical volumes. We also apply our prescription to Seifert manifolds, which are off-shell in AdS$_3$ gravity but admit dS$_3$ saddles, and find agreement with their spherical volumes semiclassically. Finally, using Dehn surgery on torus knots and links, we obtain partition functions on smooth spherical three-manifolds.

title: From bulk flows to boundary generators and costs
summary: Holographic complexity admits a broad family of bulk observables, yet their relation to boundary state-preparation costs remains unclear. We propose a local prescription that associates suitable bulk observables with quadratic cost geometries on families of states prepared by Euclidean sources. Building on the holographic transport of bulk Hamiltonian flows to Euclidean preparation sources, we use the Hessian of the transported generator at a stationary reference state to define a candidate cost metric. When this Hessian is positive definite, the minimised preparation energy reproduces the change in the bulk observable to quadratic order. We characterise the resulting preparation penalties relative to the Fubini-Study metric and compute them for the maximal volume in scalar perturbations of AdS$_3$. At large-conformal dimension, we recover the known proportionality between cost and Fubini-Study metrics. At finite dimension, we obtain positive but generally unequal penalties for source variations that displace the bulk field and its conjugate momentum, breaking this proportionality even for a single scalar operator. We further study a deformation of volume by quadratic scalar and gradient terms in the large-dimension regime, determining how the couplings modify the penalties and constrain positivity. These additions selectively change field-displacement costs, with the gradient term introducing mode dependence. Our results provide an explicit local connection between the choice of bulk observables and the assignment of boundary preparation penalties.

title: Pressure in Wilsonian effective field theory
summary: We study the exponential rolling tachyon solution in Wilsonian effective field theory as a model for rolling tachyons in open string field theory. Although this solution exhibits runaway oscillations towards the future similar to its counterparts in string field theory, its pressure is shown to be consistent with the underlying bare theory, but only up to a finite time. The rest of the evolution of the pressure is instead governed by a solution that is oscillatory towards the past and regular at late times. We conjecture that the late time physics of rolling tachyons in open string field theory may be captured by the solutions that are different from the standard rolling tachyon solutions based on this analysis.

title: Defect flows from functional relations in the asymptotic semiring
summary: We study perturbations of topological defects by a relevant holomorphic defect field in two-dimensional conformal field theory. This produces translation invariant defects and these necessarily flow to topological defects in the infrared. Translation invariant defects form a monoidal category which extends the fusion category of topological defects. We argue that the renormalisation group flow defines a semiring homomorphism from the semiring of translation invariant defects to an "asymptotic semiring" which we construct from topological defects. The semiring homomorphism preserves functional relations, and we illustrate in the example of Virasoro minimal models that the resulting relations in the asymptotic semiring constrain the defect flow endpoints. The companion paper [1] contains a detailed study of such defect flows in several minimal models, both numerically and analytically.

title: Collinear Gluons from Gravity: Poincaré-Birkhoff-Witt Decomposition and Twisted Intersections
summary: We give an explicit reconstruction of subleading collinear Yang--Mills amplitudes from one-graviton amplitudes in Einstein--Yang--Mills theory and its string corrections. We realize the monodromy kernel in the mixed open-closed string relation as a weighted Lie-algebraic recursion on words of gluon labels. At order $α'^r$, its output contains at most $r$ Lie factors. The Poincaré--Birkhoff--Witt (PBW) theorem decomposes the space spanned by gluon orderings into sectors whose dimensions are given by unsigned Stirling numbers of the first kind. Appropriate shuffle sums of one-graviton amplitudes extract the degree-$r$ sector, for which the string-period matrix drops out. Accordingly, we show that the reconstruction coefficients factor into linear kinematic factors over the product of bipartition factors. Finally, we express the reconstruction coefficients as twisted intersection numbers between Parke--Taylor forms and explicit forest cocycles constructed recursively from logarithmic four-point differentials.

title: Twisted scattering from Chern-Simons theory
summary: We consider boundary conditions of two-dimensional Dirac fermions which preserve a non-anomalous continuous symmetry which acts differently on the left- and right-movers. Such boundaries are equivalent to topological defects of Weyl fermions preserving the symmetry. We give a general construction of such defects for conformally-embedded symmetries using Chern-Simons theory. They always exist and can be realised as half-space gauging defects for some finite categorical symmetry. Using this technology, we compute the twist lines to which fermions become attached upon scattering through the defect, the boundary central charge of the corresponding folded boundary state, and its mod-2 valued SPT class. As applications, we first consider abelian symmetries and find agreement with known results in the literature. We then study a novel example where an $SU(2) \times SU(4) \times U(1)^2$ symmetry is preserved. In contrast to the abelian case, the twist lines are intrinsically non-invertible and belong to either a $\text{TY}(\mathbb{Z}_3 \times \mathbb{Z}_3)$ or $\text{Rep}(\mathbb{S}_3) \times \mathbb{Z}_3$ symmetry depending on whether scattering is to the left or the right.

title: Random Euclidean CFT$_2$ from Triangulated dS$_3$ Gravity
summary: We propose a random Euclidean CFT description of three-dimensional de Sitter gravity, with fixed central charge and primary spectrum but fluctuating operator product coefficients. Our construction starts from compact regions assembled from generalized hyperbolic tetrahedra. We analytically continue the gravitational amplitudes computed from these triangulations to de Sitter parameters and use them to infer OPE correlations. We recover matching normalized amplitudes from a complex Liouville cosmological wavefunction. For the tetrahedral $K_4$ filling, the non-Gaussian OPE cumulant carries an oscillatory hyperbolic-volume phase. We reconstruct the associated Lorentzian de Sitter spacetime and show that angle derivatives of this phase yield the rapidities of boost holonomies around its initial singularity. Its spacelike future boundary carries a positive-definite conformal metric, while the wavefunction obeys Euclidean conformal Ward identities. The physical CFT spectrum is organized by integer spin, and the scalar restriction of the two-chiral fusion coefficient yields the Virasoro $6j$ square. We construct a positive finite OPE ensemble that reproduces the theta normalization and Virasoro tetrahedral cumulant while satisfying the retained sphere-crossing equations.

title: Conformal geodesics and the hyperboloid at timelike infinity
summary: A description of scattering in asymptotically flat spacetimes that includes both radiation and massive asymptotic states requires control of the relation between null and timelike infinity. Motivated by this problem, we use the properties of conformal geodesics to construct an extended representation of timelike infinity in Minkowski spacetime. The construction exploits the fact that every non-null metric geodesic in an Einstein spacetime is, up to an explicit local reparametrisation, a conformal geodesic. It replaces the point $i^+$ by a hyperboloidal boundary $\mathcal{H}^+$ meeting future null infinity $\mathscr{I}^+$ at a corner $\mathcal{C}^{+}$, while fixing the location of $\mathscr{I}^+$ in the associated conformal Gaussian gauge. In this gauge, we derive the equations governing massless scalar and spin-$2$ fields. In particular, we obtain a transport equation for the scalar field along future null infinity and analyse the asymptotic behaviour of its spherical-harmonic modes near timelike infinity. We also derive the explicit massless spin-$2$ equations in this gauge. Finally, we examine the relation to projective extensions and to the hyperbolic base of the extended Carrollian space $\mathrm{Ti}$. Our results provide a geometric framework for studying the connection between late-time and null asymptotics which is a prerequisite for scattering constructions relevant to flat space holography.

title: General-purpose equations of state for hadron-quark matter: first application to accretion-induced phase transitions in neutron stars
summary: Strong first-order phase transitions in the cores of neutron stars (NSs) can have profound implications for astrophysical observables, however, their existence remains an open question. Since most NSs form in binary systems, they are expected to experience prolonged episodes of mass accretion that gradually increase their central density and can potentially trigger such a transition. This might, in turn, generate observable multi-messenger signals, as suggested by previous studies. Motivated by this prospect, we generate a new set of equations of state for hadron--quark matter with first-order phase transitions of various strengths, including neutrino absorption opacities in the quark phase as well. We then perform general-relativistic radiation hydrodynamics simulations of NSs undergoing accretion-induced phase transitions. In contrast to previous findings, our results indicate that these systems do not produce unbound ejecta for the models considered, making accretion-induced phase transitions unlikely sources of observable electromagnetic transients. However, we find that transitions are accompanied by intense neutrino emission, with peak luminosities reaching $\sim10^{52}~\mathrm{erg/s}$ for the strongest transition considered. To facilitate future numerical studies, we make the family of equations of state and neutrino opacities used in this work publicly available, enabling the systematic exploration of the role of the phase transition strength.

title: Wormhole geometries and energy conditions in linear and non-linear $f(Q,L_m)$ gravity
summary: This study explores static and spherically symmetric wormhole configurations in an extended formulation of symmetric teleparallel gravity governed by $f(Q,L_m)=α(-Q)+βL_m $ and $f(Q,L_m)= -Q+L_m^α $ (where $Q$ is the non-metricity scalar, $L_m$ is the matter Lagrangian, and $α, β$ are constants). By varying the action with respect to the metric, we obtain the corresponding field equations. We conclude that the linear $f(Q,L_m)=α(-Q)+βL_m$ framework successfully supports physically realistic wormholes without requiring extreme energy condition violations.
