Expanding the transverse electromagnetic vector potential into discrete single-photon frequency-comb supermodes, we show that tracing out the unmeasured continuous-wave idler field yields an exact spatial dephasing Lindblad master equation whose decoherence rate is governed by the non-orthogonal state overlap of single-photon-added coherent states. Connecting this open-system map to free-vector-space quotient measurement theory, we demonstrate that single-particle interference arises from the geometric projection of the composite state onto detector-defined conditional cosets rather than remote collapse, establishing strict operational equivalence across pump, seed, and signal phase scans. The resulting wave-particle-entanglement triality equality $P^2 + E^2 + V^2 = 1$ is saturated across the complete parameter space, while the atomic-clock-referenced comb structure anchors continuous-variable time-frequency displacement stabilizers directly at the hardware layer. Our work unifies induced coherence, Bohr's complementarity, and quotient measurement theory, providing a microscopic pathway toward fault-tolerant bosonic quantum information processing.

title: Microscopic Bipartition and Macroscopic Symmetry in a Rényi Entanglement Ensemble
summary: Universal information extracted from entanglement at a critical point is commonly associated with the long-distance properties of the bulk state, while microscopic details of a lattice bipartition are expected to be washed out under coarse graining. Counterintuitively, we show directly that such microscopic information can survive in the statistical ensemble that determines the second Rényi entropy and obviously change the physics there. Using quantum Monte Carlo simulations of the square-lattice $J$-$Q_3$ model at the Néel--valence-bond-solid (VBS) transition, we measure magnetic and dimer order parameters in the Rényi-2 ensemble. For a standard axis-aligned bipartition, the VBS component perpendicular to the entanglement boundary remains finite in the thermodynamic extrapolation and is inequivalent to the parallel component, while the Néel order vanishes. For a $45^\circ$ tilted bipartition, in contrast, the two VBS components remain equivalent within numerical accuracy. We interpret this contrast in terms of the Rényi twist defect: the two bipartitions have the same bulk theory but realize different microscopic defect symmetries. Our results demonstrate that lattice information invisible to the bulk continuum theory alone can remain active in the long-distance Rényi ensemble, providing a microscopic explanation for the strong bipartition dependence previously observed in entanglement studies of deconfined criticality.

title: Hybrid Lattice Surgery between Smooth Boundaries
summary: We develop smooth hybrid lattice surgery for group surface codes, enabling joint logical measurements through merge and split operations along smooth boundaries. The code patches may correspond to identical or different finite groups, including non-Abelian groups. Our central result is that smooth merge and split realize a logical $K$-coset measurement, where $K$ is the subgroup defining the interface. This generalizes the joint logical parity measurement of ordinary surface codes. Using a tensor-network representation, we derive explicit measurement circuits and develop procedures for correcting nonidentity measurement outcomes. We illustrate the framework through a generalized controlled multiplication gate between group surface codes and protocols for preparing the $T$, $CZ$, $CCX$, and $CS$ magic states, producing resources encoded in one or more $\mathbb{Z}_2$ surface code patches. Our results show how smooth hybrid lattice surgery broadens the range of logical operations available for group surface codes.

title: Collision-aware Bayesian mitigation of photon loss in linear optical quantum circuits
summary: Photon loss is the dominant noise source in linear optical quantum circuits. Each lost photon turns an ideal n-photon outcome into a pattern with fewer photons, so the detector counts no longer follow the ideal output distribution, and the lossless events that do follow it become exponentially rare as the photon number grows. Discarding the lossy events (postselection) therefore wastes most of the data at realistic loss rates, and the ideal distribution has to be inferred from the lossy counts themselves. Recycling-based mitigation (Mills & Mezher, Quantum 2026; Quandela's photon_recycling) reweights lossy samples to recover lossless probabilities, but its estimators are biased and restricted to the no-collision sector, where each output mode holds at most one photon. We instead treat the raw counts as Multinomial observations under per-photon binomial loss and infer the ideal output distribution and the loss rate jointly from a Bayesian posterior, which extends naturally to outputs with collisions. On data from the independent Perceval simulator at the scale of prior work (n=4 photons in m=20 and m=10 modes), the posterior has lower KL divergence than both recycling and postselection at every tested loss rate in the no-collision benchmark. In the collision regime it recovers the loss rate and the collision-pattern probabilities, which recycling cannot estimate, and stays below recycling at every loss rate and below postselection except at low loss, where the two are comparable. Its advantage over recycling grows with the sample count, and it supplies credible intervals that the baselines lack.

title: Systematic Truncated Wigner Approximation for Open Spin Systems Reveals Long-Range Order Far from Equilibrium
summary: Long-range interactions can protect dissipative order against fluctuations, but determining when they do so in two dimensions remains out of reach for existing many-body methods. We develop a continuous SU(2)-covariant truncated-Wigner framework that maps the problem onto stochastic dynamics with one Bloch sphere per site. Derived systematically from the exact Stratonovich-Weyl evolution of the Lindblad equation, it generates both drift and reservoir noise for arbitrary spin $S$. Benchmarks against exact and tensor-network calculations validate its description of non-equilibrium dynamics and steady states. Applied to 400-site two-dimensional dissipative anisotropic XY lattices, our method reveals physics missed by mean-field and perturbative approaches: vortex-antivortex proliferation destroys the predicted staggered-XY phase for nearest-neighbour coupling, whereas algebraically decaying interactions stabilize an extended $\mathbb{Z}_2$-ordered phase. We obtain the first beyond-mean-field steady-state phase diagram of the long-range interacting model, revealing reentrant loss of order at strong coupling and closure of the ordered region beyond $α\approx 3.5$. Our new method provides a scalable route to strongly correlated driven-dissipative systems with long-range interactions, higher-dimensional geometries, spin-boson couplings, and spins beyond one half, relevant to modern experiments with magnetic atoms and polar molecules in optical lattices and tweezer arrays.

title: Field demonstration of a self-contained 10 km mobile-to-ground quantum network node via common-aperture co-propagation
summary: In this work, we demonstrate a dual-function, common-aperture free-space optical system that simultaneously supports decoy-state BB84 quantum key distribution (QKD) at 803 nm and bidirectional classical laser communication at 640/660 nm over a 10.31 km terrestrial link from a mobile platform to a stationary ground station. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first field demonstration of a fully integrated common-aperture architecture where a co-propagating classical optical link simultaneously performs full QKD post-processing and ecrypted payload transmission over a 10 km atmospheric channel. The classical link utilizes Manchester-coded on-off keying (MC-OOK) at 10 MHz, achieving a packet error rate of $\sim$ 0.4 $\%$ (estimated bit error rate (BER) of 3.13 $\times$ 10$^{-5}$) with hardware-based self-synchronization and error-packet retransmission. Over the 10.31 km link, the QKD system achieved an average quantum bit error rate (QBER) of 2.512 $\%$ and an average secret key rate of 644 bps using rate-adaptive low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes. Finally, using the distilled keys, real-time AES-256 encrypted image transmission was executed over the co-aligned classical optical channel, proving the feasibility of a completely self-contained, jam resistant mobile quantum optical network.

title: Quantum algorithm for high-dimensional nonlinear stochastic differential equations based on Carleman linearization
summary: Addressing nonlinear numerical problems in quantum computing remains challenging, but several approaches, including Carleman linearization (CL), have been proposed to construct quantum algorithms for such problems. In this work, we develop a CL-based method for a high-dimensional nonlinear stochastic differential equation (SDE) $\mathrm{d} \mathbf{X}_t = \left(A(t) \mathbf{X}_t + F(t) \mathbf{X}_t^{\otimes s}\right) \mathrm{d} t + B(t) \mathrm{d} \mathbf{W}_t$ for an $\mathbb{R}^N$-valued random process $\mathbf{X}_t$, aiming at quantum speed-up with respect to the dimension $N$. We introduce auxiliary processes $\mathbf{Y}^j_t$ that approximate $\mathbf{X}_t^{\otimes j}$, derive a linearized system of SDEs for them, and obtain the linear ordinary differential equation (ODE) governing their expectations. We then apply a quantum ODE solver to it and, from the resulting quantum state, extract an estimate for the expectation of a linear function of $\mathbf{X}_t$ by overlap estimation. We show that, provided the nonlinear and noise terms in the SDE are sufficiently small relative to the linear term, the CL error decreases exponentially with the truncation order $J$ in CL, and we can estimate the target expectation with a ${\rm polylog}(N)$ number of queries to unitaries encoding coefficient matrices $A$, $F$, and $B$. Finally, we also run a numerical demonstration for an SDE related to Langevin dynamics, observing the exponential decay of the CL error as $J$ increases.

title: Geometry-Agnostic Data-Driven Discovery of Extreme Scenarios
summary: We introduce a two-stage data-driven neural framework for discovering dynamically admissible extreme scenarios. Rather than assuming prior knowledge of the governing equations, the first stage infers the effective dynamical constraints directly from observational data. When the underlying physical system possesses suitable symmetries, the learned dynamics can be represented in a geometry-agnostic form, independent of any fixed grid, coordinate system, dimensionality, and intrinsic curvature. In the second stage, a physics-informed neural-search uses this learned dynamics to uncover rare, high-impact coherent structures that may not have appeared in the original observations. We demonstrate this framework through representative examples of increasing dimensionality and geometric complexity. Starting from a traditionally learned Duffing dynamics, we find a homoclinic pulse as a plausible localized extreme scenario. Next, since the same equation also appears in the stationary nonlinear Schrodinger system, with the coordinate interpreted as space instead of time, this pulse becomes a standing soliton. We then retrain the first stage using a geometry-agnostic neural representation, enabling the learned dynamics to be lifted to higher-dimensional space to obtain higher-dimensional solitary profile, known as Townes soliton. Finally, with a Liouville system, we demonstrate that dynamics learned from data on a (1+1)-dimensional Lorentzian quasi-manifold can be transferred to a (2+0)-dimensional Euclidean manifold to identify an instanton. Our approach can be applied to other coherent spatiotemporal structures, including kinks, rogue waves, compactons, peakons, and potentially even singularities, with applications in risk analysis, nonlinear forecasting, and anomaly detection.

title: A twisted Marchenko lemma and applications
summary: We develop a twisted Marchenko lemma with applications into non-commutative two-component integrable systems. Starting from a twisted differential equation, we introduce the corresponding two-component Wronski matrix $W_{n,m}(\boldsymbolφ,\boldsymbolψ)$. Under the Marchenko lemma conditions, the logarithmic derivative $(\partial W_{n,m})W_{n,m}^{-1}$ satisfies nonlinear equations, whose two-component projections yield a non-commutative two-component KP equation, while a single-component reduction recovers the non-commutative Burgers equation, KP equation and DS equation. A direct approach based on two-component quasi-Wronskians is developed, from which a higher-order non-commutative two-component KP equation is generated with matrix-valued solutions. Reductions of the seed functions of the non-commutative two-component KP hierarchy yield the one-component counterpart, while a stepwise reduction of those for the two-component KP equation gives the non-commutative DS and NLS equations.

title: DeHNSSo-v2: A compressible, curvilinear, and efficient extension of the Delft Harmonic Navier-Stokes Solver
summary: We present DeHNSSo-v2, a major update of DeHNSSo-v1 (Westerbeek et al., Comput. Phys. Commun. 302, 2024), the open-source Delft Harmonic Navier-Stokes Solver for nonlinear stability analysis of shear flows. The new release adds a compressible formulation on general two-dimensional body-fitted geometries, automatic grid generation, linear-cost sparse assembly, reusable per-mode factorizations, and Newton pseudo-arclength continuation for high-amplitude nonlinear solutions. The curvilinear formulation preserves the fourth-order accuracy of the discretization on strongly distorted grids, and the compressible solver is confirmed to reproduce DeHNSSo-v1 in the incompressible limit. Validation spans published benchmarks for linear instability of compressible flat-plate boundary layers from $\mathrm{Ma}=0.5$ to $\mathrm{Ma}=4.5$, nonlinear oblique-mode breakdown at $\mathrm{Ma}=1.6$, nonlinear swept-wing crossflow compared with direct numerical simulations, and linear Tollmien-Schlichting wave interaction with a modeled surface-embedded Helmholtz resonator compared with experimentally validated linearized Navier-Stokes simulations. On the nonlinear test cases of DeHNSSo-v1, the computational developments result in a speed-up of approximately one order of magnitude. By broadening the scope and reducing the cost of DeHNSSo-v1, DeHNSSo-v2 provides the boundary-layer-transition and flow-control community with an accessible tool for studying receptivity, nonlinear disturbance evolution, and instability interactions with complex surface geometry and metamaterials across compressibility regimes.

title: Random $C^*$-subalgebras
summary: Given a discrete countable group $Γ$, we introduce the concept of random subalgebras of the reduced group $C^*$-algebra $C_r^*(Γ)$. This extends the existing theory of invariant random subgroups and the one of invariant random subalgebras of the group von Neumann algebra ${\rm L}(Γ)$. As applications, we provide a characterisation of $C^*$-simplicity, a condition for amenability of the group and show the existence and uniqueness of a maximal nuclear $Γ$-invariant unital $C^*$-subalgebra of $C^*_r(Γ)$. Moreover, we give a topological characterisation of exactness of any separable unital $C^*$-algebra. Finally, we study exotic random subalgebras of $C^*_r(Γ)$ and super-exotic random subalgebras of ${\rm L}(Γ)$, that is, random subalgebras which do not arise purely from random subgroups of $Γ$ and not from random subalgebras of $C^*_r(Γ)$, respectively.

title: Acceleration of CTQMC via Denoising Diffusion Models with Auxiliary Spectral Functions
summary: Continuous-time Quantum Monte Carlo (CTQMC) impurity solvers are a numerically exact, but expensive, option for solving the Dynamical Mean Field Theory (DMFT) equations, with statistical noise from undersampling presenting a major challenge to low temperature studies. This noise is especially egregious within the sampled self-energy, which can destabilize the self-consistency loop upon insertion into the Dyson equation. In this work, we introduce a neural denoiser for fermionic imaginary time Green's functions based on the diffusion model architecture trained on synthetic data. The network predicts positive and normalized auxiliary spectral functions consistent with the noisy imaginary axis CTQMC data, which is then refined via autodifferentiation to match the measured self-energy, its first two high-frequency moments, and impurity occupation similar to the Constrained Residual Minimization (CRM) method. This leads to Green's functions and self-energies that are causal by design. Through this denoising framework we are able to reduce the required CTQMC measurement steps by a factor of 10-100. We benchmark our method with a half-filled Hubbard model on a Bethe lattice, a two-patch Dynamical Cluster Approximation (DCA) of the two-dimensional Hubbard model, and the SrVO$_3$ system. We reproduce the Mott transition upon increasing Coulomb interaction for the half-filled Hubbard model with only 5000 CTQMC measurements, the pseudogap transition for the DCA two-dimensional Hubbard model with only 5$\times$10$^5$ measurements, and match the spectral function of SrVO$_3$ with 50 times fewer measurements than the reference. Since we generate auxiliary spectral functions, we recover the approximate spectral functions of the systems for free without performing analytic continuation.

title: Classical spin liquids in the kagome Ising model, and their link with magnetoelasticity
summary: We investigate a nearest-neighbor Ising model on the kagome lattice coupled to elastic lattice distortions. By integrating out the lattice degrees of freedom, we derive an approximate spin-only description in terms of a kagome \(J_1\)-\(J_2\)-\(J_{3}\) Ising model with interactions extending to third nearest-neighbors. Using tensor network methods complemented by classical Monte Carlo simulations, we revisit its zero-temperature phase diagram and characterize the ground states studied more than thirty years ago. We discover three phases with extensive zero-temperature entropy and algebraically decaying spin correlations. Importantly, these states are not confined to fine-tuned points or frontiers between phases, but occupy extended areas of parameter space. Their quasi long-range order is reflected in Bragg-like peaks in the structure factors; we relate this, and other properties, to diverse phases found in Ising and Heisenberg models. Finally, we trace the trajectories generated by the magnetoelastic coupling through the effective-model phase diagram, explaining the emergence of self-frustration for the unfrustrated magnetoelastic model with ferromagnetic interactions.

title: Neural Network Fractional Quantum Hall States with Learnable Orbital Pair Matrix Factors: Balancing Physical Priors and Flexibility
summary: Neural network fractional quantum Hall (FQH) states offer a promising alternative for capturing Landau level (LL) mixing and for understanding FQH physics, yet the incorporation of physical priors has so far been limited to the minimal exact constraints built into the ansatz. Working in spherical geometry, we show that the network's flexibility suffers both when only minimal additional physical priors are supplied and when priors such as flux attachment are imposed rigidly. In the former case, the monopole harmonic product orbital (MHPO) ansatz is difficult to optimize, whereas in the latter, the expressivity of the neural network is restricted. We therefore propose the orbital pair matrix factor MHPO (MHPO-M) ansatz, which balances physical priors against flexibility by not only replacing the fixed Laughlin structure with learnable pair factors but also making them dependent on both the electron configurations and the orbitals. Across $ν=1/5$, $1/3$, and $2/5$, MHPO-M achieves the lowest variational energy among the tested variants, and a factorized orbital readout based on it enables scaling to 35 electrons, with energies competitive with trends inferred from three-LL exact-diagonalization results. These results demonstrate that physical priors can be appropriately incorporated without sacrificing the flexibility of neural network wavefunctions, opening a promising path toward accurate, scalable modeling of FQH systems with LL mixing.

title: Finite-temperature spectral functions of lattice polarons with process tensors
summary: We develop a process tensor approach for calculating the finite-temperature spectral functions of lattice polarons. We show that the finite-temperature phonon influence functional can be expressed as the elementwise exponential of a low-rank matrix product state, enabling an efficient summation of electron worldlines. An embedding construction embeds worldlines of different propagation times into a single matrix product state. This construction yields the propagator over the full simulated time interval in a single calculation. We benchmark this approach against available finite-temperature density-matrix renormalization group results for the one-dimensional Holstein polaron. We further obtain numerically converged spectra for the two-dimensional Holstein polaron. The spectra reveal a progressive transfer of spectral weight from coherent spectral features into an incoherent background with increasing temperature.

title: Stable and causal frames for BDNK hydrodynamics
summary: We establish the existence of families of linearly stable and causal Bemfica-Disconzi-Noronha-Kovtun (BDNK) frames for arbitrary equation of state and set of physical transport coefficients. By developing a method based on simplification of Routh-Hurwitz criteria and telegrapher factorisation of polynomials, we provide six concrete examples of such families, three of which admit conformal limits, for both neutral and charged fluids. These frames have adjustable characteristic speeds and can serve as a starting point for numerical implementations of relativistic hydrodynamics in various settings. In the process we uncover a map between stable and causal frames in neutral fluids and stable and causal frames in charged fluids. We also develop an AI research protocol that can be used to search for such frames in any hydrodynamic theory.

title: "Massive" Conformal Field Theories and application to Nambu-Goto string
summary: I describe the recent progress in understanding diffeomorphism invariant two-dimensional theories with dimensionful parameters which have nevertheless traceless improved energy-momentum tensor and turn out to be conformal invariant. An example is the Liouville theory with the additional four-derivative terms arising from the Nambu-Goto string and telling apart the Nambu-Goto and Polyakov strings. Its exact solution in embedding dimension d=4 is consistent in contrast to the Polyakov string and described by the (4,3) unitary minimal model. Talk at Irina Aref'eva Conference "Perspective Directions in Quantum Field Theory and Superstrings", Moscow 12-17 October 2026.

title: Circling in on correlation functions in $\mathcal{N}=2$ orbifold theories
summary: We review the harmonic superspace formalism for 4d $\mathcal{N}=2$ theories and apply it to orbifolds of $\mathcal N=4$ Super-Yang-Mills (SYM) theory. These theories have a remarkably similar description to $\mathcal N=4$ SYM, but their planar supergraphs feature topological twist lines which generate phases when intersecting bifundamental hypermultiplet propagators. These cause twisted sector BPS correlators to depend on the coupling $g$. Twisted Coulomb-branch operators of length $L$ receive a leading perturbative contribution to their two-point function at order $\mathcal{O}(g^{2L})$ from a supergraph involving a wrapped hypermultiplet circle. After performing the complete $D$-algebra, we show that the supergraph reduces to the universal conformal period $W_L=\binom{2L}{L}ζ(2L-1)$. We extend this analysis to multiple nested hypermultiplet circles and show that they reproduce a series of higher-order terms in the exact localisation result. A subsequent evaluation of leading contributions to BPS three-point correlators again shows complete agreement with localisation results in extremal case and generates new perturbative data in the non-extremal case. The latter involves one untwisted BPS descendant, which contains physical hypermultiplet fields and can therefore connect directly to the twist-dependent hypermultiplet circle. This reduces the suppression in $g$, resulting in a contribution $4 g^{2(\ell+1)} W_{\ell+1}$ controlled by a bridge length $\ell$ rather than by an external operator length $L\geq\ell$. These examples demonstrate the feasibility of harmonic superspace calculations in orbifold theories and point to various future applications in the context of non-BPS correlators, integrability and marginal deformations.

title: Orientifold and Integrability: $\mathcal{N}=4$ Super-Yang-Mills on $\mathbb{RP}^4$
summary: We study planar $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang-Mills theory (SYM) on the real projective space $\mathbb{RP}^4$ using integrability, holography and supersymmetric localization, and discuss its relation to orientifolds in string theory. We show that the integrability of $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM is preserved when combining the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ involution defining $\mathbb{RP}^4$ with the action of the charge conjugation of the SU$(N)$ gauge group. We demonstrate this by calculating one-point functions of non-BPS single-trace operators in various subsectors at weak coupling, which can be mapped to overlaps between energy eigenstates and crosscap states in integrable spin chains. The results exhibit a parity selection rule, a hallmark of integrability, and are given in terms of a ratio of determinants. Building on these results, we conjecture a closed formula for general single-trace operators. We further provide evidence that this construction is holographically dual to a probe orientifold O1-plane in $\text{AdS}_5\times \text{S}^5$ by constructing the corresponding worldsheet crosscap states in the pp-wave limit. Finally, we use supersymmetric localization to compute one-point functions of half-BPS operators exactly at finite $g_{\rm YM}$ and $N$. The computation reduces to two-dimensional Yang-Mills theory on $\mathbb{RP}^2$ twisted by charge conjugation and leads to a matrix integral of a Wishart-Laguerre type. In the planar limit, the exact result interpolates between the weak-coupling gauge-theory result, the strong-coupling supergravity prediction for the orientifold, and the worldsheet crosscap in the pp-wave limit.

title: de Sitter Gluon Correlators in Momentum Space
summary: We show a new diagrammatic representation of tree-level wavefunction coefficients for gluons in four-dimensional de Sitter space at any multiplicity. Its ``disc diagrams" make the cutting rule manifest, while the remaining contact term is fixed by the absence of folded singularities. We determine this term for configurations with zero, one and two negative-helicity gluons. It simplifies as more gluons share a helicity, and it vanishes for all-plus. We illustrate the expansion at four and five points, attach explicit results up to eight points all-plus, and relate it to Grassmannian residues.

title: De Sitter Observers and an Effective Field Theory of Horizon Edge Modes
summary: We show that choosing a test observer in $dS_D$, specified by the framed embedding of their horizon $S^{D-2}$, spontaneously breaks the de Sitter and internal sphere isometries to diagonal rotations. We identify gravitational edge modes, described by low diffeomorphism jet fluctuations near the horizon sphere, as the associated Goldstone modes. We construct their membrane-like effective theory, organized in a small-gradient expansion. We find a class of nonlinear actions that at the quadratic order reproduce the edge-mode spectrum previously found in the one-loop gravitational $S^D$ path integral.

title: Twisted Correlators from Harmonic Superspace
summary: We establish a harmonic superspace formulation for $\mathcal N=2$ orbifolds of $\mathcal N=4$ super-Yang-Mills (SYM) theory. We account for the orbifold projection by introducing topological defect lines to the planar supergraphs of $\mathcal N=4$ SYM. These twist lines are sourced by twisted sector operators, transparent to vector multiplets but generate orbifold phases when crossed by bifundamental hypermultiplet fields. This formalism establishes a refinement of the orbifold inheritance principle at supergraph level. As a direct application, we compute leading twist-dependent corrections to BPS two- and three-point functions, finding agreement with localisation results in extremal cases and generating new data for non-extremal correlators. We further map these corrections to finite-size effects in the twisted hexagon formalism. This opens a path towards an all-order integrability prescription of orbifold structure constants.

title: Digital Quantum Simulation of Dynamics in Interacting Fields
summary: Matter under extreme conditions behaves as a non-equilibrium, strongly-interacting quantum system. Such systems are in the non-perturbative regime of quantum chromodynamics (QCD), where their time evolution is classically intractable. Quantum computing offers a promising alternative, but present-day devices are limited in qubit count and circuit depth, so efficient formulations and algorithms are key to scaling toward experimentally relevant QCD simulations. A scalable framework is established for simulating energy loss and hadronization in 1+1-dimensional SU(2) lattice gauge theory, in which a heavy quark traverses a lattice of light quarks. Classical lattice QCD methods are translated into physics-informed circuits to prepare the interacting ground state. The evolution is run on IBM's quantum processor ibm_pittsburgh, where the charge distribution and energy loss are measured. A further study develops the quantum simulation of the fully gauge-fixed SU(2) Hamiltonian in a mixed basis, a formulation that is expected to remain efficient at all gauge couplings. Digitizing the continuous gauge fields with as few as three qubits per plaquette reproduces low-energy observables with $10^{-3}$ precision. Scaling to larger systems is limited by resource overhead, which motivates truncations that preserve the relevant observables. Sequency Hierarchy Truncation (SeqHT) exploits the hierarchy in basis-operator contributions. Demonstrated on the adiabatic preparation of the $λφ^4$ ground state on ibm_sherbrooke, SeqHT reduces circuit depth by ~30%, suppressing hardware noise in the extracted observables. All simulations in this dissertation are validated on quantum hardware against classical benchmarks. These studies advance quantum simulations of real-time QCD dynamics.

title: Can Quantum Layers offer Performance and Security Advantages in Vision-Language Models?
summary: As quantum computing moves from the noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) era toward early fault-tolerant quantum computing (EFTQC), quantum-enhanced AI is shifting from a conceptual idea to experimental research. Quantum components are expected to extend the capabilities of existing AI systems, yet it remains unclear how such components will help within large multimodal models. In this study, we try to answer that question for vision-language models (VLMs) using classically simulated quantum layers. With LLaVA-OneVision as the backbone, we evaluate 4- and 8-qubit basic-ring and strongly entangling circuits at four insertion and four replacement locations. Insertion adds quantum layers to the classical model, while replacement substitutes them for classical components. Using the same setup, we compare performance and computational cost between classical and quantum-classical hybrid models. On the Visual Spatial Reasoning dataset, inserting a quantum layer after the visual projector reaches 80.7% development accuracy, 2.28 percentage-points above classical full fine-tuning. Replacing the final decoder feed-forward sublayer retains 79.22% accuracy with 13.07 million fewer trainable parameters. Quantum insertion can thus improve accuracy, and selective replacement can reduce parameters. These benefits depend strongly on where the quantum layer is inserted or which classical component it replaces: earlier replacements lower accuracy, and fewer parameters do not reliably shorten training or reduce computation. To assess potential security benefits, we evaluated the robustness of quantum-classical hybrid models under six attack settings. Overall, our study maps where quantum layers help and hurt within VLMs, offering a starting point for hybrid VLM design; whether these gains generalize remains open. The code is available at https://github.com/TITANS-Lab-Artifacts/QuantumVLM.

title: From Qubit Tensorization to Gaussian Optimizers in Bosonic Systems
summary: We develop a method for deriving Gaussian optimality results for bosonic quantum systems from inequalities for qubit systems. Inspired by Gross's derivation of the Gaussian logarithmic Sobolev inequality from an inequality on the two-point space, we use qubits as quantum two-point spaces and lift bosonic Weyl operators to pseudo-Weyl operators on large qubit systems. By controlling weighted norms and relative entropy in the fluctuation limit, we establish two transfer theorems that convert tensorized qubit inequalities into inequalities for bosonic Gaussian channels. As a first application, we prove that the sharp $2$-logarithmic Sobolev inequality for the bosonic Ornstein--Uhlenbeck semigroup tensorizes without loss in the constant. We also establish a sharp output entropy inequality for tensor powers of a class of qubit channels. This includes a quantum Mrs.~Gerber's lemma determining the minimum output entropy of tensor powers of the qubit depolarizing channel at fixed input entropy. Applying our relative entropy transfer theorem, we obtain multimode constrained minimum output entropy bounds for Gaussian additive-noise channels and thermal attenuators in the heating range.

title: Engineering Low-Latency, High-Throughput Quantum Decoders on NVIDIA GPUs
summary: We design and optimize a quantum error correction (QEC) decoder for NVIDIA GPUs, combining Relay belief propagation, a state-of-the-art message-passing algorithm, with order-zero ordered statistics post-processing. Our implementation uses CUDA Graphs to control GPU execution, stops updates for converged samples, and collects unresolved samples in queues for post-processing. We optimize sparse traversal through coalesced message accesses, prefetching, and register reuse, and accelerate binary post-processing with warp-level collectives. In addition, mixed FP16-FP32 arithmetic and INT8 quantization reduce message storage and traffic while retaining accuracy using accumulators at higher precision. We evaluate surface, hypergraph product, and bivariate bicycle code workloads on NVIDIA A100 and GH200 data-center GPUs and a commodity RTX 5080. On the bivariate bicycle code at error probability 0.003, INT8 halves amortized decoding time relative to independently tuned FP32 with a negligible logical error rate increase on RTX 5080. With independent syndrome batches submitted back-to-back to concurrent decoder instances, RTX 5080 delivers 91% of GH200's highest measured throughput with an 8.9x shorter median submission-to-correction latency. The combination of performance optimization, mixed precision, INT8 quantization, and concurrent decoder instances opens a path toward QEC decoder clusters built from commodity GPUs.

title: Pushing beyond the memory barrier in propagation algorithms with randomization
summary: Performant classical tools for simulating quantum circuits are important for benchmarking and supporting upcoming quantum devices. Pauli propagation offers promising capabilities, but deep circuits usually cause a rapid growth in the number of Pauli strings and can quickly exhaust the available memory. In this work, we introduce a randomized protocol that combines a specialized resampling schedule, merging, and a controlled amount of bias to keep the propagating Pauli sum within any prescribed memory budget. Additional computational resources can then be spent on embarrassingly parallel repetitions that systematically improve the estimate. Building on the open-source library PauliPropagation.jl, we show that 1) increasing memory of each simulation reduces the error systematically more than outside averaging, 2) resampling just enough to apply the next gate delays variance accumulation and gives better error-per-time trade-offs than more aggressive resampling, and 3) a small, controlled bias is crucial in cutting down variance and pushing far beyond unbiased randomization. The resulting framework can reproduce deterministic calculations while requiring several orders of magnitude less memory.

title: Bias-Preserving Entanglement of Kerr-Cat Qubits with an ATS Coupler
summary: Kerr-cat qubits offer a hardware-efficient route to fault-tolerant quantum computing by suppressing bit-flip errors exponentially, while phase-flip errors increase only linearly with the mean photon number. To maintain this protection, entangling operations must be bias-preserving, ensuring that phase-flip errors occurring during the gate do not propagate into bit-flip errors. In this paper, we propose an asymmetrically threaded SQUID (ATS) parametric coupler to implement high-fidelity, bias-preserving entangling gates between Kerr-cat qubits. By engineering a photon-number asymmetry between the control and target modes, we enable fast gate operations that suppress non-adiabatic leakage without complex pulse shaping. Through numerical simulations of the full circuit Hamiltonian, we demonstrate a bias-preserving CX gate achieving 99.69% fidelity in the absence of photon loss for a gate duration of 50 ns. Under a single-photon loss rate of 100 kHz, our protocol yields a noise bias of 9922, exceeding the noise bias of a naive non-bias-preserving CX implementation by approximately a factor of 570. These results support the ATS coupler as a valuable building block for concatenated cat-qubit architectures.

title: CoDecoder: Make Quantum Decoders Up to 100x Faster and Even More Accurate
summary: Fault-tolerant quantum computers need fast and accurate error decoding. We present CoDecoder, a small neural frontend that composes with an existing decoder to improve accuracy and reduce mean decoding time. It predicts each shot's logical outcome, retains confident predictions and routes the remaining shots to the unchanged fallback. A logical-operator-aware output head scores shifted logical operators, combining equivalent logical lines on surface codes and deciding logical qubits jointly on bivariate-bicycle (BB) codes. Fused GPU inference and efficient routing reduce the overhead paid on every shot. In registered tests under circuit-level noise, composition reduces failures by 6.4-31.4% relative to correlated matching on surface codes of distance 7-17 and by 22-50% relative to full-DEM Relay-BP on two BB codes, with 2.3-124-fold speed-ups across these comparisons. With our re-implementations of the neural decoder Cascade, composition reduces decoding time in all four settings. A joint decision of both decoders on the routed shots keeps this speed and makes the composition more accurate than Cascade in all four, with 14-18% fewer failures on the [[72,12,6]] code. On the [[72,12,6]] BB code, a conventional head with independent logical outputs fails 3.8-5.0 times as often as our joint class score under matched training conditions. Per-shot analysis shows how composition gains accuracy. On retained shots, the frontend corrects more fallback errors than it introduces, even when it is less accurate overall.

title: Local Clifford equivalence to CSS codes: Polynomial-time classification and conversion
summary: Calderbank--Shor--Steane (CSS) codes support decoding and fault-tolerant logical operations through separate pure $X$ and pure $Z$ stabilizer checks. Generator choices and single-qubit Clifford transformations can obscure this structure. We give a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm that decides whether an arbitrary stabilizer code is locally Clifford-equivalent to a CSS code and constructs the required transformation and CSS checks whenever such a form exists. For $m$ possibly redundant generator rows on $n$ qubits, the algorithm uses $O(mn^2+n^4)$ binary field operations. We reduce the problem to affine linear systems by characterizing local projectors that preserve the span of the binary stabilizer labels. The conversion preserves code parameters and check sparsity for quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes. We demonstrate CSS recovery and decoder reuse and resolve previously open LC-to-CSS classification questions for published code constructions. For graph states, LC-to-CSS equivalence corresponds to the existence of a bipartite graph in the local-complementation orbit. We derive a necessary-and-sufficient adjacency-matrix criterion for this property and construct such a graph whenever one exists. Our algorithm makes CSS decoding and fault-tolerant constructions accessible throughout the local Clifford equivalence classes of CSS codes.

title: Separability does not certify zero-noise extrapolation: Factorial diagnostics in dynamic quantum circuits
summary: Separately amplifying gate, latency, and mid-circuit measurement errors can simplify zero-noise extrapolation, but a weak interaction between amplification knobs does not establish an accurate zero-noise limit. We distinguish observable separability, response-model adequacy, and calibration of that limit, and test them in a pre-specified $2^3$ factorial experiment on three IBM dynamic circuits. For the primary echoed spectator observable, the latency-measurement coefficient is $b_{LM}=+0.0007$ with a nominal 95% bootstrap interval $[-0.0033,+0.0049]$. A separately planned follow-up meets a $\pm0.005$ equivalence criterion and recovers two injected interactions; both repeat runs nevertheless trigger the drift rule. Multi-knob extrapolations have smaller median absolute errors than the single-knob comparisons, yet all five original strategies exclude the known ideal value for three of six observables. Duration controls support a model-dependent contribution to the spectator deficit from unequal decay rates in native padding and added delay. We give an explicit construction showing why measurements at two measurement-knob levels cannot identify the extrapolated limit without response assumptions. A post-hoc precision analysis and an additive full-factorial estimator expose a further bias-variance trade-off hidden by point-error comparisons. The experiment provides a diagnostic of the implemented response surface, not a certification of physical channel independence or mitigation accuracy.

title: Mechanical angular momentum loss at $\mathcal{O}(G^4)$ from static and radiative gravitons
summary: We determine the loss of mechanical angular momentum $L^μ_{\rm loss}$ of two gravitationally scattering bodies at $\mathcal{O}(G^4)$ using worldline quantum field theory (WQFT). The gravitational memory effect, a phenomenon of the early- and late-time behaviour of the gravitational field, leads to static contributions to $L^μ_{\rm loss}$. We illuminate how these arise: the linear memory contributes through so-called static correlators, while the nonlinear memory vanishes at this order due to symmetry considerations. The computation of the remaining, dynamical part resembles that of the $\mathcal{O}(G^4)$ impulse. We generate its integrand using a reformulation of the WQFT Feynman rules that conserves four-momentum at every vertex and plainly exhibits the classical loops. The three-loop integrals are reduced to master integrals, whose differential equations and boundary matching in the post-Newtonian limit we describe in some detail. In contrast to conservative effects at this order, only polylogarithms appear. While individual contributions to the dynamical part are divergent, these cancel in $L^μ_{\rm loss}$. The quadratic-in-radiation part of our result reproduces earlier results, while the complete result agrees with existing post-Newtonian results.

title: Large-Level Limit of Doubled Chern-Simons Theory Part I: Regular Sector, Boundaries and Interfaces
summary: We study three-dimensional $BF$ theory as the large-level limit of the doubled Chern--Simons theory $G_k\times G_{-k}$ for simply connected, compact, simple $G$, a limit that connects the symmetry topological field theories of finite and continuous symmetries. Lines whose two highest weights grow linearly with $k$ at fixed difference become $BF$ lines, with magnetic flux set by their average and electric charge equal to their difference. Representing level-$k$ torus states as normalized flux--charge wave packets, we prove that every fixed modular transformation of any fixed normalizable state with regular flux converges in the strong-$*$ topology to its $BF$ counterpart. The Dehn twist gives each line exactly its Aharonov--Bohm phase at every level, while $S$ converges to a Fourier transform exchanging flux and charge, without escaping to singular holonomies or large charges. States that approach singular fluxes at large $k$ are not covered. The natural boundary 2d theory is speculated to be a decompactified boson in the abelian case $G=U(1)$, and $\dim G$ non-compact free scalars for general $G$. For $SU(2)$, we discuss the gapped interfaces between adjacent levels, which must shift some flux or charge by a finite amount. In the $k\rightarrow\infty$ limit the interface is conjectured to be the $c=1$ Runkel--Watts theory.

title: A new class of rotating black hole solutions endowed with a scalar hair
summary: We present new hairy stationary and axisymmetric black hole solutions. These solutions belong to a subclass of Horndeski scalar-tensor theories, in which there is no non-minimal coupling to curvature. The full rotating solutions are obtained numerically using the Kadath library based on spectral methods. The metric does not rely on an explicit ansatz but rather on the use of a set of numerical coordinates. Black holes obtained differ from Kerr in general, and depend on a new independent parameter, a primary hair, coming from a linear time dependence in the scalar field. These solutions admit a Killing horizon like the Kerr black hole, but are non-circular, and break the zeroth law of black hole thermodynamics.

title: On Integrable Deformations of CFTs and Integrable Two-Dimensional Sigma Models
summary: In this paper, we analyze the systems of screening charges corresponding to $η$-deformed $O(N)$ and $OSp(N|2m)$ sigma models. These sigma models can be represented as integrable deformations of certain conformal field theories. Based on the case of $O(N)$ sigma models, which were conjectured in previous works by A.V. Litvinov and co-authors to be an integrable deformation of the conformal field theory corresponding to the algebras $W(D(n+1|n))$ and $W(D(n|n))$ for the cases $N=2n+2$ and $N=2n+1$ at $n \geq 1$, respectively, we formulate a hypothesis on how to write down the system of screening charges for the conformal field theory whose integrable deformation defines the $η$-deformed $OSp(N|2m)$ sigma model for the case of odd $N=2n+1$, asymptotically free models with $N-2m-2>0$ and $n \geq 2$, $m \geq 1$. This hypothesis is explicitly verified for the cases of $OSp(5|2)$, $OSp(7|2)$, and $OSp(7|4)$, which were separately investigated in the work of M.N. Alfimov and co-authors.

title: Cosmological perturbations from localized sources: a gauge-invariant multipolar theory
summary: We develop a first-principles description of the linearized gravitational field of localized sources in spatially flat Friedmann-Lemaître-Robertson-Walker universes with arbitrary smooth expansion histories. The construction determines the complete retarded metric and the induced perturbation of the surrounding cosmic fluid from prescribed source stresses and a cosmologically stationary past field. It includes all multipole orders and accounts for curvature tails, through which the field depends on the source's past history inside the light cone. Generalizing the Blanchet-Damour multipolar formalism, we identify gauge-invariant mass and current moments together with a canonical cosmic fluid moment that determines an independent scalar response. This response vanishes in Minkowski and pure de Sitter spacetime, although curvature tails persist in de Sitter. The gauge-invariant multipoles are obtained directly in position space. This gives an exterior description without the nonlocal spatial projection through the source interior required by the usual scalar-vector-tensor decomposition. We also relate the canonical multipole metric to the standard variables of cosmological perturbation theory. The retarded construction requires neither a slow-motion nor a geometric-optics approximation. We define effective multipolar sources by truncating the moments of slowly varying sub-Hubble extended sources at a prescribed Cartesian multipole order, recovering the earlier quadrupolar and octupolar models in de Sitter spacetime. We recover the known Minkowski and de Sitter multipolar fields and obtain an analytical representation for gravitational propagation in the $Λ$CDM model including radiation.

title: Local Measurement Theory for Quantum Cellular Automata
summary: The formulation of quantum measurements compatible with relativistic causality is obstructed by the tension between the locality of observable algebras and the dynamical state transformations induced by measurement processes. We develop a local measurement theory for quantum cellular automata, lattices of finite-dimensional quantum systems with a causal reversible dynamics evolving in discrete time steps. Measurement processes are described by localized completely positive maps and organized into operational measurement protocols, finite non-adaptive sequences of local instruments distributed across the causal cone induced by the automaton local dynamics. Each protocol induces an effective measurement on the initial time slice, whose support is constrained by the causal structure generated by the automaton. Non-local measurement effects therefore arise through causal propagation and composition of local operations, rather than from primitive non-local interventions or instantaneous collapse prescriptions. We establish the corresponding spatial support bounds and characterize the resulting measurement architecture. As an explicit example, we construct a two-step protocol for a one-dimensional nearest-neighbour qubit automaton which, for suitable automaton parameters, realizes a Bell-basis projective measurement on two neighbouring sites after coarse-graining of the local outcomes. Away from this point, the same protocol generates a continuous family of deformed Bell measurements whose entanglement and stabilizer Rényi non-classicality can be quantified explicitly. The framework thus provides a causally consistent operator-algebraic mechanism for synthesizing spatially extended quantum measurements from strictly local operations.

title: U(1) Current Diffusion in Gauss-Bonnet Holography
summary: We study holographic $U(1)$ charge transport using a probe Maxwell field in a five-dimensional Gauss-Bonnet-AdS black-brane background. Within the all-order linearised fluid/gravity framework, we derive the off-shell constitutive relation and determine the diffusion function and electric and magnetic conductivities analytically in the hydrodynamic regime and numerically at generic frequency and momentum. To first order in the Gauss-Bonnet coupling, the leading diffusion constant remains unchanged in our normalization, while its frequency dependence and the electric conductivity receive nontrivial corrections. The deformation also generates a nonvanishing leading magnetic conductivity. Beyond the hydrodynamic regime, it modifies the transport profiles while preserving the damped behaviour of the diffusion function. The corresponding memory kernel vanishes at negative times, supporting a retarded constitutive response.

title: Construction of Causal Set Propagators in $2+1$-Dimensional Constant-Curvature Spacetimes from Two-Link Paths
summary: We study a link-based retarded scalar propagator on causal sets sprinkled into $2+1$-dimensional Minkowski, anti-de Sitter, and de Sitter spacetimes. The construction is based on the squared link matrix $\mathbf{L}^2$, whose expectation value counts two-link paths between fixed endpoints. In the high-density limit, the dominant contribution localizes near the intersection of the null boundaries of the Alexandrov interval, and the flat-space normalization remains unchanged in constant curvature. The resulting kernels agree with the corresponding continuum Klein-Gordon propagators for a nominally massless scalar with effective curvature coupling $ξ_{\rm link}=1/6$. Since the conformal coupling in $2+1$ spacetime dimensions is $1/8$, this value is not a conformal-coupling effect. Together with link-based results in $1+1$ and $3+1$ dimensions, where the same coefficient $1/6$ appears, this suggests that the coupling may reflect an ultraviolet property of the link structure, reminiscent of the combination $(1/6-ξ)\mathcal{R}$ in local heat-kernel expansions.

title: Black hole free energy landscapes from constrained instantons
summary: We apply gravitational path integral factorization to provide a semiclassical interpretation of generalized black hole free energy landscapes at fixed external temperature and angular velocities. Boundary integral transforms express the formal partition function as an integral over constrained sectors labeled by complete local partial-Neumann data on an auxiliary hypersurface. Independent variation establishes paired regular subregion solutions as constrained instantons, with Lagrange multipliers supporting lapse and tangential shift jumps that accommodate thermal and rotational mismatches. For selected nonextremal stationary families with an asymptotic boundary, the constrained saddle action takes the form $I_{\rm constr}=β\mathcal F_{\rm gen}=β(E_{\mathcal B}-Ω_{\mathcal B}^{I}J_{\mathcal B,I})-S$, with $β=T^{-1}$. Here $E_{\mathcal B}$ and $J_{\mathcal B,I}$ are renormalized Hamiltonian charges and $S$ is the black hole entropy, whose contribution to the action comes from the regular horizon cap. Interior stationary points of the landscape correspond to smooth equilibrium saddles when the retained variations independently span the entropy and angular momentum directions. We extend the construction to local, parity-even $f(\mathrm{Riemann})$ theories without curvature derivatives by retaining the complete auxiliary interface data. The same thermodynamic form follows with Wald entropy, without a small-deficit expansion. Schwarzschild and Kerr black holes illustrate the Einstein construction, while five-dimensional static AdS black holes in Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet gravity and the rotating BTZ branch of new massive gravity provide explicit checks of the higher-curvature extension.

title: The Geometry of the "Gauge Argument"
summary: We show how the "gauge argument", widely criticized by philosophers as ad hoc and unconvincing, may be reconstructed rigorously, and, we believe, convincingly, as an argument concerning the geometry of vector bundles. In this form, the gauge argument has two parts, the first of which is strongly analogous to the Weyl-Stein argument for Galilean spacetime as the appropriate setting for Newtonian gravitation; and the second of which invokes a classic result in the Yang-Mills theory literature, due to Utiyama [1956, "Invariant Theoretical Interpretation of Interaction", Phys. Rev. 101, 1597].

title: Interferometric trilemma for ultraviolet-softened gravity
summary: Ultraviolet-softened extensions of general relativity can weaken gravity at short distances, whereas a positive Källén--Lehmann spectral density forbids gravity from falling below Newtonian strength. Which property of the mediator must such a weakening sacrifice? For Lorentz-invariant Gaussian mediators coupled linearly to the conserved stress tensor, we formulate three independent interferometric conditions that jointly imply this bound: visibility is never amplified, decoherence is fixed by the energy radiated by the difference source, and no interferometer responds to a later one. At tree level, the three ghost prescriptions of quadratic gravity each violate exactly one: negative-norm ghosts amplify coherence, negative-energy ghosts decohere without positive energy transfer from the difference source, and a time-symmetric fakeon response produces advanced fringe shifts. Any universal short-distance weakening of gravity therefore certifies that its mediator violates one of these conditions, and the observables proposed to certify quantum gravity become consistency tests of its ultraviolet completion.

title: Gravitational Instability of Cold Axion Dark Matter Beyond Minimal Coupling
summary: Following recent observations of unexpectedly massive galaxies at high redshift by the James Webb Space Telescope, the revision of Dark Matter (DM) models --specifically regarding how DM couples to gravity-- has become a central topic in Cosmology. In this paper, we develop an axion model for Cold Dark Matter (CDM) with a non-minimal coupling to gravity. From this framework, we evaluate the gravitational instability in the hydrodynamic limit. Our results demonstrate how gravitational instabilities depend on the non-minimal coupling parameter, providing a novel tool for aligning with the high-redshift observations from the James Webb Space Telescope.

title: One-loop unifying relations between Yang-Mills theory and the nonlinear sigma model from Berends-Giele currents
summary: We study unifying relations between Yang-Mills theory and the nonlinear sigma model. We extend tree-level amplitude relations expressed through differential operators to off-shell multiparticle currents and obtain one-loop integrand relations by sewing two off-shell legs. This off-shell approach may also apply to higher-loop integrands.

title: Higher-Dimensional Test of the Holographic Dual of Entanglement Cohomology
summary: We extend the holographic test of entanglement cohomology from $d=2$ to higher-dimensional conformal field theories. For a $d$-dimensional CFT with a spherical entangling region $A$, the vacuum modular Hamiltonian is known explicitly, and the boundary relative entropy of a primary-operator perturbation can be computed via conformal Ward identities. On the bulk side, the perturbation is dual to a scalar field in AdS$_{d+1}$, and the bulk canonical energy is computed using the JLMS relation. We carry out the computation explicitly for $d=3$ and $d=4$ and find that the boundary and bulk results agree at first order in the perturbation, with identical coefficients $κ_d Δ^2 / C_T$, where $κ_3 = π^2/12$ and $κ_4 = 3π^3/16$. The result extends the quantitative verification of the holographic dual of entanglement cohomology beyond the $d=2$ case treated in the companion paper and confirms that the modular Hamiltonian perturbation is the correct holographic image of the first entanglement cohomology class. We discuss the role of the conformal anomaly, the shape of the entanglement wedge, and an outlook on TsT-deformed backgrounds. \keywords{Entanglement entropy \and Cyclic cohomology \and von Neumann   algebras \and Holography \and Modular Hamiltonian}

title: The long-range Ising CFT: perturbative and nonperturbative approaches
summary: The long-range Ising model is the prototype of criticality with power-law interactions. In each dimension its interacting critical points form a one-parameter family of nonlocal conformal field theories, weakly coupled at both ends but not in between. We study this family in one, two and three dimensions from several independent directions. We extend the expansion about the generalized free field from three to eight loops and expand about the short-range end. We show that Hamiltonian truncation applies to this nonlocal theory once a truncation artifact is corrected. Where they can be compared, the resummed expansions, Hamiltonian truncation, the numerical renormalization group and Monte Carlo simulations agree on the dimension of the leading $\mathbb{Z}_2$-even scalar at the sub-percent level, as universality requires.

title: Subsystem quantum Rényi-Bhattacharyya distance in 2D CFTs and its holographic applications
summary: We develop a systematic method to compute the subsystem fidelity and Rényi fidelity in two-dimensional conformal field theories (CFTs) from the operator product expansion of twist operators, and apply it to the subsystem quantum Bhattacharyya distance (BD) and Rényi-Bhattacharyya distance (RBD). We validate the method against exact results in the free massless fermion and boson theories, and then use it to compute the BD and RBD in holographic CFTs between two heavy primary states, between two thermal states, and between a heavy primary state and a thermal state. When the two states differ in their classical, order-$c$ data, the distances are of order $c$, and the states are distinguishable already at the level of classical gravity; when the leading data coincide, the distances are of order $1/c$ at every order of the short interval expansion, so that the distinguishability becomes a perturbative quantum gravity effect. For a heavy primary state and its thermal counterpart, the leading contribution to the BD appears at order $\ell^8$ and is of order $c^0$, whereas the RBD is generically of order $c$, in line with the earlier finding that a heavy primary state and a thermal state share the same order-$c$ entanglement entropy but have different order-$c$ Rényi entropies in the short interval expansion.

title: Spectroscopy as a Probe of Spacetime Foam
summary: Quantum-gravitational spacetime foam varying in space and in time imprints, respectively, a transverse phase decoherence and an achromatic, stochastic arrival-time jitter on light from distant sources. We show that the jitter modifies the first-order temporal coherence $g^{(1)}(τ)$ and hence the observed spectrum, providing a spectroscopic probe of the temporal variation, complementary to existing imaging-channel constraints on the spatial variation. In the dynamical-foam limit, where the foam decorrelates within the light's coherence time, the spectrum splits into a coherent line core suppressed by $e^{-σ_φ^2}$, with $σ_φ^2$ the variance of the foam-induced phase jitter, and an incoherent pedestal, yielding a spectral shape-distortion bound on the foam exponent $α$. Three probes follow: the outright survival of broadband flux, the fractional width of a spectral line, and a chromatic deficit across a broadband continuum. Applied to the MeV emission lines of GRB\,221009A we obtain $α\gtrsim 0.63$, a weak, lever-arm-dominated floor. For the broadband CMB the foam induces an $e^{-σ_φ^2(ν)}$ deficit ($σ_φ^2 \propto ν^2$); a fit to the COBE/FIRAS monopole spectrum reaches $α\gtrsim 0.52$ ($95\%$ CL), and next-generation spectrometers reach only $α\gtrsim 0.54$--$0.55$ (forecast), limited by the foam--temperature degeneracy. The pedestal-independent line-width and CMB bounds are floors below the holographic value $α= 2/3$, consistent with and excluding no part of the imaging window reported for GRB\,221009A; only the conditional TeV survival bound ($α\gtrsim0.74$), which holds only for near-Planck-refresh foam ($τ_{\rm foam}\lesssim4\times10^{-28}$\,s), would exclude it --- and, with it, the window.

title: Primordial black holes in braneworld gravity: A gateway to hidden dimensions and the dark Universe
summary: This thesis investigates the cosmological dynamics of primordial black holes (PBHs) within the Randall--Sundrum Type II braneworld scenario. The work comprises a preliminary discussion on gravitational collapse in the small-black-hole limit at early cosmological epochs, and two principal studies. The first study presents a fully relativistic treatment of PBH accretion in the early Universe, employing Michel accretion theory within the covariant Shiromizu--Maeda--Sasaki formalism. The analysis reveals that higher-dimensional effects substantially enhance early-time accretion onto light PBHs, with discrepancies between our black hole masses and previous estimates growing with cosmic time as $t^{0.33}$ --- a difference that reaches several orders of magnitude by the end of the strong-accretion epoch. This finding fundamentally alters the mapping between the initial PBH mass spectrum and present-day populations. The second study reassesses the observational and cosmological constraints on higher-dimensional PBHs in Randall--Sundrum cosmologies. Constraints from direct Hawking radiation, unresolved diffuse gamma-ray backgrounds, microlensing surveys, and energy injection into the cosmic microwave background are reanalysed in light of the modified higher-dimensional evaporation dynamics and updated observational surveys. Taken together, these results identify viable regions of parameter space in which PBHs can account for the entirety of dark matter while remaining consistent with current observational bounds. Notably, due to the enhanced accretion epoch, PBHs capable of constituting a significant fraction of dark matter may originate from masses below the effective four-dimensional Planck scale. This thesis thus puts forward a dark matter candidate with a distinct evolutionary history and observational signatures today.

title: Quantum algorithms for optimal control: large-scale finite-horizon linear-quadratic regulation
summary: We develop quantum algorithms for optimal control over a prescribed finite time interval (finite horizon), focusing on continuous-time linear-quadratic regulation (LQR). This foundational control problem often requires solving a nonlinear matrix Riccati equation, which can be costly for large systems and long control durations on conventional classical solvers. We instead work directly with the state-costate optimality equations, reformulating the LQR problem as a multiple-shooting linear system. Importantly, we prove a condition-number bound for the system that is independent of the horizon, under stabilizability and detectability assumptions. By incorporating the initial and final conditions into a single linear system, we can solve the subsequent linear system more efficiently with a quantum linear systems subroutine. For a given initial state, our quantum algorithms return classical estimates of the optimal cost and the optimal control inputs at a selected time, without constructing a Riccati solution operator. Given sparse-matrix block-encodings, an initial-state preparation oracle and a fixed number of control inputs, the query and gate complexities scale polylogarithmically with system size and control duration, provided that sparsity, relevant norms, and stability parameters are bounded. The dependence on the target error is inverse-linear up to logarithmic factors. We establish the required bounds uniformly in system size and duration for a family of damped mass-spring chains with two endpoint controls. Numerical experiments support the analysis.

title: Supervised Learning with Quantum Hamiltonian Embeddings
summary: Machine learning is widely regarded as a promising application in which quantum computing could offer a computational advantage. However, general quantum machine learning models with provable guarantees on performance, trainability, and efficient inference remain limited. In this work, we introduce quantum Hamiltonian embeddings, a supervised learning framework in which a classical training dataset is encoded into a single effective, parameterized Hamiltonian. Training optimizes the parameters of this data-dependent Hamiltonian, whose approximate ground state defines the classification rule. Once the ground state has been approximated using a quantum algorithm, inference can be performed either classically using a classical representation of the learned state, or with a quantum representation of the state. We establish efficient methods for gradient estimation and prove favorable generalization guarantees. Furthermore, under standard cryptographic assumptions, we show that Hamiltonian embeddings can realize hypothesis functions beyond the reach of efficient classical algorithms. We then demonstrate the framework at scale on IBM Heron processors using a standard benchmark dataset. Together, these results establish Hamiltonian embeddings as a new framework for quantum machine learning, combining theoretical guarantees with a path for experimental investigations at scale on quantum hardware.

title: Correlated decoding loses the surface code's effective distance below threshold
summary: Correlated decoding improves matching and clustering surface-code decoders by reweighting one decoding subgraph conditioned on the other's correction. We show that standard reweighting can cause correlated decoders to fail on size-$(d-1)/2$ fault configurations that a distance-$d$ code should correct, reducing error suppression deep below threshold. Under circuit-level noise, a single first-pass edge can discount several correlated edges, even though their joint occurrence requires additional independent faults, so the decoder favors an over-discounted correction. Regularizing the reweighting rule restores the nominal distance scaling and a clear correlated-decoding advantage.

title: High-Accuracy Propagation-Assisted Local Decoding for Fast Transversal Clifford Circuits
summary: We benchmark the Iterative Redecode Scheme (IRS) on fast transversal Clifford circuits, achieving high-accuracy correlated decoding using local memory-style detectors and decoders. On a deep random Clifford benchmark, IRS yields approximately $4\times$ lower logical failure rates than the ghost protocol at $d=11$ with matched buffers, and $15\times$ lower rates than logical observable matching (LOM). In three-block GHZ preparation, IRS achieves $2\times$ lower logical error rates than reliable logical Pauli-product decoding with matched initialisation, improving to $25\times$ at $d=19$ with $\lceil d/2\rceil$ full initialisation rounds. We place IRS, which builds on Wan et al.'s scheme, within a broader propagation-assisted local (PAL) framework, where local decoders exchange messages rather than decoding a global hypergraph. IRS alternates local minimum-weight perfect matching (MWPM) on memory-equivalent detector error models (DEMs) with Pauli-frame propagation and detector updates across transversal CNOT layers, seeking local error estimates consistent with the global detector record. Prior-informed DEMs account for probabilities of propagated errors missing from the memory-equivalent model, improving initial decoding and reducing logical error rates. Zero-weight physical Pauli mechanisms enable inference and propagation of initially indeterminate stabilizer outcomes. Error rates saturate after a few iterations even for deep, adversarial alternating-tCNOT circuits, allowing iteration caps with negligible loss of accuracy. We find syndrome-extraction buffers of order $\lfloor d/4\rfloor$ sufficient for distance-dependent error suppression in the demanding regimes studied. The approach extends to other local decoders and CSS codes; for repeated logical $S$ gates, IRS achieves approximately $4$ to $10\times$ lower logical error rates than LOM, depending on initialisation.

title: A General Master Equation for Two Accelerated Detectors: Stationary States and Entanglement
summary: We derive a general Gorini-Kossakowski-Lindblad-Sudarshan master equation for two co-located, uniformly accelerated two-level detectors weakly coupled to scalar fields in the Minkowski vacuum, retaining coherent and dissipative contributions for arbitrary orientations, field masses, and spacetime dimensions. For equal orientations, we determine stationary states and their entanglement for two couplings to massless fields in four dimensions: symmetric coupling yields acceleration-dependent concurrence, whereas rotating-wave coupling gives acceleration-independent concurrence.

title: Phase-sensitive quantum-state texture during thermalization of a Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya Heisenberg dimer
summary: We investigate quantum-state texture during the thermal relaxation of an anisotropic spin-$1/2$ Heisenberg dimer subject to a longitudinal magnetic field and a Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya (DM) interaction. Starting from local transverse and longitudinal couplings to a bosonic bath, we construct a global weak-coupling Lindblad equation, identify its transition channels, and discuss the applicability and limitations of the secular approximation. The Gibbs state is obtained explicitly in the local spin basis, revealing that the DM coupling controls both the modulus and phase of the single-excitation coherence by modifying the energy splitting and rotating the chiral phase. For heating and cooling protocols, we compare rugosity, fidelity-based texture, and trace-distance texture with coherence, vector spin chirality, and purity. The relaxation dynamics separates population thermalization from the decay and precession of deliberately prepared energy-basis coherence. Their combined contribution to local coherence produces DM-dependent texture overshoots and, during cooling, damped oscillations and sign changes of the coherence quadratures. These transients differ from the evolution of coherence magnitude and purity, while trace-distance texture weights them differently from the overlap-based quantifiers. Calculations at reduced dissipation preserve the texture maxima within the secular model. The results identify a phase-sensitive diagnostic of relaxation.

title: Non-Markovian exceptional points and information backflow: a Heisenberg reaction-coordinate approach
summary: The primary pathway to the investigation of exceptional points (EPs) in open quantum systems has been the use of Markovian master equations. However, recently it has been realised that they can arise in settings that show non-Markovian behaviour. The main approach in this direction has been the use of pseudomodes, which allow the influence of a structured environment to be replaced by new damped auxiliary modes. In this work, we use a Heisenberg-equation approach which relies on the reaction-coordinate formalism to obtain exact analytical dynamics. First, we show how our method considerably simplifies the analysis compared to the use of master equations. Second, we utilise it to discuss non-Markovian revivals in systems with second and higher-order EPs, showing that the notion that EPs demarcate the onset of revivals is not generally true. We then utilise our results to discuss the dynamical effects of higher-order non-Markovian EPs, deriving bounds on the number of revivals and investigating enhanced asymptotic relaxation near higher-order EPs. Finally, we investigate non-Markovian EPs with engineered reservoirs and show how they can be utilised to control the rate of irreversible information loss.

title: Exploring ground state phase diagrams of Rydberg atom arrays with finite projected entangled-pair states
summary: Rydberg atom arrays (RAA) have been advocated as a promising avenue for the quantum simulation of different exotic quantum states. Numerical predictions for the ground state properties of this experimental platform can, however, be challenging in two-dimensional setups. In particular, faithfully treating long-range interactions is often crucial for distinguishing the fate of competing phases, but it usually comes at considerable cost. Projected entangled-pair states (PEPS), optimized via a sampling-based approach, have been shown to deal with such terms on the same ground as shorter-range ones. In this work, we employ these tools to investigate debated physical questions in different frustrated geometries of RAA, from the emergence of spin-glass physics on the Kagomé lattice to topological order beyond the PXP model on the Ruby lattice. By that, we contribute to establishing PEPS as well-suited tools for creating digital twins of RAA experiments.

title: End-to-End Optimization of Partial Fault Tolerance in Neutral-Atom Arrays
summary: Fault-tolerant (FT) quantum computation offers a pathway to quantum advantage, but its realization is hindered by its significant overhead. The partially FT "STAR" architecture reduces the cost of universal computation at the price of relaxing FT requirements for non-Clifford operations, increasing exposure to hardware noise. Therefore, maximizing its performance and applicability demands careful co-design with the underlying hardware. In this work we investigate the co-design of the STAR architecture with neutral-atom platforms, connecting the underlying atomic physics to logical error modeling and application-level performance. At the physical level, we identify a favorable noise bias in $^{171}\mathrm{Yb}$ Rydberg gates, and show how it can be enhanced through error-selective pulse optimization. At the logical level, we identify an intrinsic error suppression mechanism, yielding vanishing logical coherent noise in leading order. Detailed circuit-level simulations of surface code implementations show more than an order of magnitude reduction in logical error relative to previous estimates. As a concrete target application, we focus on the Fermi-Hubbard model with periodic boundaries, for which we design a simulation circuit particularly suited to early implementations. We quantify the resource tradeoff of partially and fully FT approaches to gate synthesis, with the former showing approximately an order of magnitude reduction in state-injection depth, and an even larger reduction in Clifford resources. Comparing with classical and fully FT approaches, we identify regimes where partial fault tolerance provides both lower overheads and lower error rates. In our estimates, this is accessible with moderate error rates $p\sim 10^{-3}$ and a few thousand qubits, underlining that for these types of problems, partial FT approaches provide a compelling pathway to early quantum advantage.

title: Higher-order Parity Constraints for Quantum Approximate Optimization
summary: The Parity Architecture was originally introduced in the context of quantum optimization algorithms to overcome hardware connectivity constraints. Here, we show that its benefits extend beyond this role by identifying specific parity transformations that enhance the success probability of the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) for optimization problems defined on hardware-native and sparse graphs. Numerical simulations suggest that this enhancement originates from the higher-order operators introduced by the Parity representation, which accelerate the propagation of correlations across the physical device. We investigate this mechanism for the Signed Max-Cut problem on 3-regular graph instances and demonstrate its practical relevance on IBM Heron quantum processors. QAOA parameters are first classically optimized on small training instances containing up to 14 vertices and subsequently transferred to larger instances executed on quantum hardware.
